and two metadata routes (`forgetCancelledReg`, `releaseSettledVoidReservationsLocked`), an
abandoned admission and a destruction without evidence all removed entries while the
client might still hold the PUBLISH. At Receive Maximum 1 that sent a second PUBLISH under
the client's first (Spec5 [4.9]). The owner is now the **custody ledger**
(`outbound_custody_ledger.go`), one per generation, and a map removal releases nothing it
does not hold.

**Two kinds of entry, disjoint removal rules.** An ADMISSION reservation belongs to one
`admitInflightPublish` call; an EXCHANGE entry to one admitted lineage. They live in
separate maps because a create's allocation nonce is its lineage: both stand under one
string from the landing until the admission settles.

- The admission reservation is opened in the SAME critical section that moves the tracked
  allocation out of the scheduling projection (the entry's `custody` flag), so the slot is
  never uncounted; an allocation already abandoned before that point is not admitted at
  all. It is removed only when the ladder has returned AND every attempt it submitted is
  settled. The ladder retries without passing the delivery gate again, so a reservation
  released between attempts would let another delivery take the slot while a retry lands
  beside it. The write callback runs synchronously inside the ladder, so "the ladder
  returned" also covers an attempt still inside its operation.
- Each submitted attempt is recorded as an immutable `{handle, lineage}` pair and settled
  by the protocol every F-105 attempt uses: resolve the handle; if unresolved, take the
  attempt's outcome subject with the create-only abort and resolve again. Landed charges
  the lineage THAT attempt wrote (the ladder's record is rewritten between attempts);
  positively never-landed drops the attempt; still unresolved stays on the reservation for
  the reconciler. A refusal before composition sent nothing and records nothing.
- An exchange entry is removed only by an exact read of that exchange at an ENDED phase —
  `mqttExchangeCharge`'s definition, the one the substrate already stated — or by
  generation discard. Ended phases are absorbing and the exchange subject is create-only
  per lineage, so an ended read releases whenever it was taken. A pending-drain phase
  holds (output may still execute); `Publish` and `PubRecObserved` hold (a successful
  PUBREC keeps the quota); an absent or unreadable exchange holds (an absence is not a
  fact).

**Hints never release.** The acknowledgement advance (on every outcome), the drain
completion, a withdrawal, and a landed pair replacement (for the superseded lineage)
schedule an exact observation on the ledger's single-flight custody dispatcher. A
continuation that stopped on absence or a successor says only that the exchange MAY have
ended. When the
delivery gate, the retained-delivery gate (whose downgrade to QoS 0 would otherwise be
permanent under retained-only traffic) or the allocator withholds — including an allocator
EXHAUSTED while the ledger holds any identifier, which with no Receive Maximum is the only
withholding a stale hold produces — it also asks for a bounded re-observation pass over all
targets — exchange entries, admissions with unsettled attempts, uncertain
subjects — ordered by when each was last attempted, so a stable live entry never starves a
stale one.

**The custody dispatcher is the observer made autonomous (F-097).**
`outbound_custody_dispatcher.go` has ONE start site, `startCustodyDispatcher`, which every
hint, pass request, owed item and tick reaches. It runs only as an admitted worker
(`srv.admitWillWorker`) holding the incarnation lease, both acquired before the
single-flight flag is set and held for the whole run, so shutdown joins it; a refused
admission or lease starts nothing and the durable records carry the work. A run whose
queues keep refilling would hold that lease indefinitely, and a retirement waits for it
before the generation may change, so the loop also stops between units once the CURRENT
close cycle of its tracker is closing: the unit in flight finishes (bounded by the
per-unit request limit stated in `docs/CONFORMANCE.md`; a store that stalls it past the
drain ceiling takes the ceiling disposition every other owner does), the units it had
taken but not run go back to their queues, due, and its exit leaves everything queued.
When a closing incarnation tracker is aborted and re-admits, its `onReopen` callback
(`rearmCustodyAfterReopen`) restarts the dispatcher if anything is queued, a throttled
census included, since the closing tracker refused every start in the meantime. Each
iteration takes at most eight units, round-robin across its queues (hints, the requested
pass's targets, due retries of indeterminate exchange reads, due owed withdrawals, due
admission-continuity records), and each unit re-checks its captured generation, epoch and
ledger; the loop asks the dispatch gate after every unit. Nothing retries inline: a unit
without progress backs off from 100 ms, doubling to `max(100 ms, min(5 s, AckWait/4))`
with +/-20% jitter, and progress resets it. A read retry is cleared by a read that
returns its exchange, in any phase, and retired by a retry run that finds neither a
ledger holder nor an ACK binding left to observe (a census that observed the exchange
ended removed both). The tick is a tracked timer
(`scheduleWillTimer`, key `$MQTT_custody_tick.<client>.<gen>.<arm>`) armed for the
earliest eligible item, a latched demand or a throttled census, and its callback is the
start site. A recorder that finds a run in progress starts nothing, so the run's exit
takes as its own any hint, pass request or due item (zero eligibility is due) recorded
after its last look, and a run that may not continue arms a due item's tick, or a queued
hint's or pass's (they are always due), for now rather than dropping it. Every arm takes
a fresh key from a per-session arm identity (`custodyTickArm`) stored with its deadline,
because a tracked timer stays registered until its callback returns and the run that
callback started may need to re-arm before then; a superseded or discarded arm is
cancelled by its stored key, and a callback whose arm is no longer current starts
nothing. A withholding gate
LATCHES demand: the dispatcher records the latch's next deadline (`custodyDemandDueAt`, on
the same backoff) and requests the pass only when that deadline comes, so between
deadlines nothing is queued and the dispatcher is idle; a deadline stands until it is
consumed (another run's exit neither moves it nor backs it off). The latch is cleared
once an allocation has since succeeded with nothing deferred, or retired at its own
deadline, instead of requesting the pass, when nobody is deferred, no identifier is
unknown and no custody is held: a waiter may leave without ever being allocated (a drain,
a consumer teardown or a resume drops its deferred entry) and the retained downgrade and
allocator exhaustion defer nothing, so with none of the three standing no allocation can
still be waiting, and a later withholding latches again. The census is the one
heavy operation, history-proportional and not one of the eight units: it runs at most
once per cap interval across every trigger (`lastHeavyAt`), and the interval is stamped at
ADMISSION, so a census that fails consumes it as a successful one does: the next census
after a failure waits out the rest of the interval, whatever the store does meanwhile. An
owed withdrawal and an admission-continuity record each get ONE bounded step per unit, and
an item whose subject is decided retires at its next unit: an owed withdrawal that finds no
evidence retires once its exchange owes no further delivery (ended, delivery abandoned, or
generation discarded: an earlier attempt may have landed behind a lost response; an
unreadable exchange keeps it) or its register no longer names the allocation, and a
continuity record once its exchange owes no further delivery. Both read the one predicate
(`mqttExchangeDeliveryDutyEnded`), and only the item retires: the identifier, the ACK
binding, the register and the holds are untouched, so an abandoned delivery's identifier
stays closed and the destruction door keeps its own ended-only rule. A
generation change cancels the retiring generation's tick, drops the queues, the latch, the
owed items and the continuity records with the ledger, and makes every captured identity
fail, so the loop exits. The dispatcher never reads or writes `piSpaceIncomplete`: it
releases exchange custody, and reopening allocation after an incomplete recovery stays the
next complete resume's. So a failed read is re-read, and while a withholding gate's
demand stands a peer's later completion of the exchange holding the slot is rediscovered
without traffic; the AckWait re-offer of a withheld delivery is no longer the only driver.
Its stated cost limits are in `docs/CONFORMANCE.md`.

**Two budgets, not one number.** New QoS 1/2 work is admitted while BOTH hold: the local
scheduling budget (`len(pendingPublish)` against MaxAckPending — it paces this broker's
own scheduling, and JetStream enforces the consumer's cap itself) and, when the client
advertised one, the Receive Maximum (every ledger charge, plus the scheduling entries the
ledger does not own: experimental affine (chapter P), a retained allocation before its
admission (7c), and an ordinary or shared entry before its conversion). The resume's
replay of already-tracked deliveries
is budgeted separately: each replayed entry is already counted, so exactly its own count
comes back out while every other known occupancy stays counted; budgeting it as new work
would replay nothing at saturation, and the acknowledgements that free the capacity would
never come. Deferred, never-transmitted deliveries are new work and fill only what
remains.

**The identifier is a conjunction, checked at the allocator.** `bumpPI` hands out an
identifier only when no map entry, no ledger entry and no live send hold holds it. Because
the check is at the allocator, every exclusion-lift route and every map removal is covered
at once. One consequence: a same-identifier pair replacement over an occupant whose
exchange is still charged can no longer be reached by allocation, because the allocator
skips that identifier.

**A resume rebuilds custody from the EXCHANGES**, before any register is routed and before
delivery or allocation opens: an outstanding exchange whose register is gone — the gated
door's destruction without evidence among them — still holds its charge and identifier,
and a census of registers would not see it. The census reads exchanges only (actions do
not bear on custody), and it is conservative in every direction. A census that fails,
including one answering stream-not-found, leaves the ledger INCOMPLETE: no new QoS 1/2
work and no allocation until a later pass completes. An exchange subject that does not
decode, or is listed and then reads absent, is kept as UNCERTAIN by subject: it holds a
charge and withholds all allocation (its identifier is unknown) until an individual
re-read decodes it or the generation is discarded. A later census only adds, so it can
never forget an uncertainty by no longer listing it.

**Generation.** The ledger is replaced wholesale with the generation, and every ledger
method enters through one guard, so a late callback or census of a retired generation
changes nothing in its successor's ledger.

### A late acknowledgement is bound before it arrives

A transmitted PUBLISH whose scheduling entry is removed before the client answers used to
lose its answer: the handler found no entry and no binding and dropped the PUBACK, and the
exchange was held to the generation's discard. An acknowledgement carries a packet
identifier, not a lineage, so the binding to the exact exchange it answers has to be
captured BEFORE the entry goes, never reconstructed from whatever occupies the identifier
when the packet arrives (F-097 / F-088, `outbound_ack_route.go`).

**Every removal states why.** `untrackPublish` and `untrackPublishEntry` take a MANDATORY
`mqttUntrackReason`:

- `mqttUntrackAnswered`: the client's acknowledgement is being handled (the ACK handler,
  and `endSendWith`'s acknowledgement settlement); installs nothing;
- `mqttUntrackEnded`: the exchange positively ended (`removeLineageProjectionsLocked`,
  from an accepted ended observation); installs nothing;
- `mqttUntrackUnanswered`: every other removal. Only this reason, with
  `PossiblyAttempted` evidence, installs an AckRoute binding, in the same `sess.mu`
  section that removes the entry (`installAckRouteForRemovalLocked`). With
  `MarkerStanding` nothing is bound (a cancellation that decided it owes its withdrawal);
  with `Unknown` nothing is bound and the producing owner keeps it.

**The evidence is an enum whose zero value proves nothing.** `mqttSendEvidence` has
exactly three values: `Unknown` (the zero value), `PossiblyAttempted` and
`MarkerStanding`. The entry form (`mqttEntrySendEvidence`) is `PossiblyAttempted` only for
an acting entry this object owns that is classified possibly attempted (`transmitted`,
whether or not a marker deletion is still owed) and is not a pending store, a foreign or
marker-opaque reservation, or a cancelled placeholder; `MarkerStanding` for an acting entry
that holds its marker with no possible attempt; `Unknown` otherwise. `PossiblyAttempted` is
positive evidence of a POSSIBLE attempt, not of a local write or of wire receipt: the
entry recorded its own transmission intent, or recovery found its marker authoritatively
absent or a recovered output token beside it (below). There is no record form of this
enum: the record-side evidence, a register's marker read authoritatively absent, is the
write boundary's own read (`mqttRefutedCancellation`), and no binding is ever built from
a record.

**One binding index, two roles** (`mqttAllocationAckBinding`, keyed by generation and
identifier):

- **HandBack**: an abandoned delivery's binding (its register is `delivery_abandoned`,
  its exchange carries the abandonment fact). Terminal reconstruction is allowed, and its
  ending is matched by the abandonment fact. A SHARED HandBack also keeps the source-ACK
  gate closed, so it is removed only when its exchange ended AND its register is proven
  deleted (or on discard).
- **AckRoute**: a possibly attempted delivery whose entry was removed unanswered. It is
  built from the ENTRY (slot reference, nonce, lineage, acquisition, QoS, source), never
  from a record read; its register stays at `publish`. It ends on its lineage's ended
  observation alone, shared or not, and holds no source gate. A retained or slot-only
  (experimental affine) entry gets none: a retained register names its materialization,
  which the entry does not carry, and the slot-only class is chapter P's.

A HandBack replaces an AckRoute of the SAME allocation (the abandonment upgrades the
routing binding it found); nothing else is ever overwritten, and an AckRoute never
replaces a HandBack. A binding authorizes no output, allocates nothing and holds no charge:
the custody ledger holds those, by the exchange.

**Identity, authority and owner of an arriving acknowledgement:**

| Population | Identity carrier | Completion authority | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Acting entry, including one restored by a complete resume | the entry's slot reference | the ordinary handler path; durable steps re-validate identity and acquisition | the handler, then the terminal-retry worker (PUBACK, failed PUBREC), intent resolution (successful PUBREC) or `mqttProcessPubComp` (PUBCOMP) |
| AckRoute or HandBack binding, no live entry | the binding (allocation, lineage, acquisition, QoS, source) | `resolveAbandonedAckLocked` + `mqttAckSnapshot`, so the bound acquisition is what `intendPubRelSlot` and the terminal path check | as above, from the binding |
| Marker-opaque reservation (recovery could not decide the marker) | the reservation | none: whether the PUBLISH was sent is unknown | none on this connection; the ACK is declined, and the next COMPLETE resume replaces the reservation |
| No entry after a failed pre-apply reread | none | none | none; the ACK is dropped and the next complete resume restores the entry |
| Foreign, bodyless or mismatched reservation, or a cancelled placeholder | not this exchange's | none | declined |

The handler's no-entry case resolves either role's binding under `sess.mu`, after
`sess.c == c`, and never reads an occupant by identifier to invent one. A successful
PUBREC on an AckRoute keeps its intent semantics: its register was never re-phased, so
`resolvePubRelIntent` answers `mqttPubRelIntentStillOwed` while the register's acquisition
still equals the binding's, and the resolution worker retries `intendPubRelSlot` (at most
one whole invocation per resolver attempt); a moved acquisition is a successor
transmission, answered `Other`, never retargeted, and the binding retires.

**Removal is by proof**, through one boundary (`removeAbandonedAckBindingLocked`):
`Ended` (enough for an ordinary HandBack and any AckRoute), `EndedAndDeleted` (a shared
HandBack), `Discard` (the generation discarded by authority) and `Handoff` (recovery's
acting restore of the same allocation retires an AckRoute, so the two never both route
the acknowledgement). Removal is an exact compare-delete, so a delayed ending cannot
discharge a replacement binding.

**The ended-lineage veto.** The custody ledger records every lineage it accepted an
ENDED observation of (`endedLineages`, filled by `noteEnded`) for the generation's life,
and an AckRoute install for such a lineage is refused: ended phases are absorbing and an
exchange subject is create-only per lineage, so binding an ended exchange could only route
a later reuse's acknowledgement to an obligation that no longer exists. A HandBack is
exempt. The memory is one lineage string per ended exchange, replaced with the ledger.

**A standing marker beside outstanding output authority is not proof of
non-transmission (F-088).** The marker proves non-transmission only together with a
register that carries no token (the write boundary's rule, "Outbound in-flight
registers"): a holder whose output token is still outstanding can record intent, delete
the marker and write after any read of it. Recovery's send-state derivation
(`recoverInflightRegistersOnce`) therefore classifies a validated ordinary `publish`
register whose marker stands and which carries an `ActionToken`
(`mqttRecoveredOutputAuthority`) as POSSIBLY ATTEMPTED, and every routing decision that
may drop a register as never sent asks one predicate, `mqttRecoveredProvenUnsent`
(decided, not opaque, marker standing, not possibly attempted). Such a register stays in
the restore population: neither the genuine-cancellation arm nor the consume arm over a
non-reofferable source takes it. The marker's own disposition (`mqttMarkerInstallUnsent`)
has no token input, so it states what the marker proves and the derivation overrides it.

**The invariant that makes the recovery read sufficient.** An ordinary acquisition
(`opAcquireAction`) commits the authority transition, the action and the register token
in one atomic batch, under the acquiring connection's ACCEPTED generation and tenure at an
expected authority sequence, so once a successor tenure is accepted a displaced holder
acquires nothing more. The successor's recovery runs after its accept, and both intent
and the write need a held token. Every token under which a displaced holder can still
write is therefore visible as `ActionToken` at the successor's recovery read. A landed
acquisition whose response was lost is in the same batch and is adopted for cleanup only
(`resolveUnacquiredPublishAction`), never for transmission. The argument covers
authority-backed acquisition only: the slot-only class (chapter P) takes its token by a
standalone CAS and is excluded. The same read covers this object's own live section on a
resident repeat recovery.

**A possible attempt and a marker debt are independent facts.** `mqttRecoveredSend`
carries `transmitted` (the classification: identifier held, never released as unsent,
DUP=1 on the next send) and `markerSeq` (a standing marker the next sender must confirm
deleted before it writes) separately, and `mqttRecoveredPending` copies them
independently. A token-bearing register keeps its marker sequence as deletion DEBT: a
holder that drains without recording intent leaves the marker standing, and a later
transmission of ours that did not confirm the delete first would leave a standing marker
over a real PUBLISH, which a later recovery would read as proven unsent. A nonzero
`markerSeq` therefore means marker presence, not non-transmission. On a resident repeat
recovery an eligible same-allocation resident (`recoveredResidentEligibleLocked`: an
ordinary acting entry, not opaque, demoted, foreign or cancelled, held under custody for a
lineage that has not ended) takes the classification monotonically, keeping its marker
and any live section's captured DUP and marker; another allocation's resident is never
touched.

**Consequences, through the existing mechanisms.** `provenUnsentReleasableLocked` refuses
the entry, so no expiry, drain withdrawal, teardown purge or void staging releases it as
unsent; `drainClaimDispositionLocked` enrols it as a started delivery; an UNANSWERED
removal by any other route meets `PossiblyAttempted` evidence and installs the
allocation-bound AckRoute, whose identity, ended-lineage veto, lifecycle and release are
unchanged; and a retransmission carries DUP=1 and still confirms the retained marker's
delete before the write. A drain finishes such a delivery without a recovered
`jsAckSubject`: `finalizeDrainDelivery` releases the register, persists the claim's
removal and finishes the drain whatever the ACK subject, and only the source-ACK
submission depends on one (the in-session disposal of the drain's consumer after a failed
save is F-124's gap, `docs/ROADMAP.md`). The conservative classification's cost, a
never-written message retained and later sent with DUP=1, is stated in
`docs/CONFORMANCE.md`.

**A successful acting restoration supersedes the allocation's cancellation verdict.** A
nonce verdict says "never transmitted"; an ordinary acting entry restored on a decided,
non-opaque possibly-attempted classification (marker absent, or a recovered output token
beside a standing marker) contradicts it, and left standing the verdict would fence every
retransmission in `beginSendLocked` and strand an exchange the client may hold. In the
`sess.mu` section that installed the entry, and only after the custody-gated install
succeeded, recovery retires the nonce (`retireSupersededVerdictLocked`): on a fresh
install, and on the eligible same-allocation resident above even when that resident
already read transmitted. Never during speculative classification, on a failed install,
for an opaque reservation or for another allocation's restore. The helper frees no parked
reservation and hands off no exclusion, unlike `forgetCancelledReg`: a restoration is not
a release. It moves `voidedRegsRev` only when membership changed, so the revision-keyed
persistence (`persistVoidedRegs`) records the omission. A crash before that write, or a
fork repair's union resurrecting the nonce (the merge runs before recovery), makes the
next recovery repeat the same handoff. The `beginSendLocked` fence itself stays
unconditional: a genuine cancellation (marker standing, no output token) is proven
unsent, never reaches a restore, and stays fenced.

**`piSpaceIncomplete` gates none of this.** Its readers are the allocator and the
recovery-release and disposal-recovery gates; a bound exchange completes and releases its
custody while allocation stays withheld after an incomplete recovery. Not covered, stated
in `docs/CONFORMANCE.md`: a crash between receiving an acknowledgement and its durable
advance (R-B). A PUBCOMP answers a PUBREL entry and keeps its own owners, unchanged.
Where recovery could not decide the PUBREL side, the PUBCOMP is declined until the next
complete resume, as before; for an ordinary QoS 2 exchange the decline happens at the
recovery placeholder PUBREL entry a cold resume installs (`regRecoveryPlaceholder`),
not through `recoveryPIHeldLocked`, which that class never reaches (T29).

**A drained source records its PUBREL intent first.** When an AckRoute's successful
PUBREC answers a delivery whose source a drain still claims (a drain-owned deny
installed the binding), the handler records the drain's PUBREL intent
(`recordPubRelIntent` with the binding's nonce) BEFORE `intendPubRelSlot` moves the
exchange, exactly as the live-entry path does: the drain's claim is released only by a
confirmed PUBREL, and the canonical PUBREL is delivered only for the exchange the intent
names. Without it the PUBREL was withheld for ever and the drain stayed claimed (found by
T29 `pubrec-ackroute`).

### An admission that may have landed keeps its source

One source delivery has at most one un-ended exchange. An admission can LAND while this
broker cannot tell that it did: its response is lost, every readback of its register
fails and its custody resolution stays unresolved, so the ladder gives up and
`abandonInflightRegister` drops the entry and the source mapping. The source's next offer
was then a stranger to the session and was admitted again, under another identifier and
another lineage, while the first stood at `Publish`. Witness W5b
(`TestF097ContinuityW5bLandedThenUnreadable`) reached exactly that: two un-ended
exchanges for one source delivery. W5a (a definite failure, the batch never leaving) does
not: the re-offer is admitted once.

**The continuity record** (`outbound_admit_continuity.go`). An abandonment whose admission
the custody ledger reports landed or still unsettled (`admissionMayHaveLanded`), or whose
lineage the ledger holds an exchange for, installs an `mqttAdmissionContinuity` keyed by
the source delivery `(durable, sequence)`, in the abandonment's own `sess.mu` section,
instead of deferring the source. It carries the generation, epoch, allocation nonce,
lineage, identifier and the ADMITTING connection's licence (`mqttLicenceOf(c)` of the
ladder that gave up, the entitlement it admitted under), never the session's current
binding, which after a takeover is the successor's. Only
the ledger-admitted classes (ordinary and shared) install one: a retained copy has no
source delivery to refuse, and the experimental slot-only class has no ledger admission
(chapter P). An abandonment whose register the door destroyed after reading or making
its exchange ENDED (our own write, ended by another continuation) installs none: the
zero licence it carries authorizes nothing, and the source is deferred as before. While
the record stands, `trackPublish` refuses that
delivery's offers, keeping only the latest acknowledgement subject on the record, never in
`sess.deferred`. It is a refusal, not evidence: it authorizes no output and ends nothing
on its own say-so.

**The dispatcher owns it.** Each unit takes exactly ONE step, so each stays within its
own dispatcher row and the per-pass bound holds:

- **superseded:** a resume restored this allocation's own entry (same identifier, nonce
  and source delivery, `continuityRestoredLocked`); the entry owns the delivery, its
  retransmission and its acknowledgement, and the record retires;
- **settle:** the admission attempt is still unsettled; settle it (resolve, abort,
  resolve);
- **withdraw:** a previous classification marked the withdrawal due; ONE
  `withdrawUnsent` under the recorded licence, which reads, and whose boundary
  re-checks, the unsent marker. Landed: the obligation is ended `WithdrawnUnsent`, the
  record retires and the offer is NAKed. Unlicensed (a successor serves): the record
  retires and the successor's recovery classifies the obligation under its own licence
  (withdrawn where its source is gone, restored as an unsent acting entry over a live
  source). Any other outcome: the mark is cleared and the next unit re-classifies (the
  register may have moved);
- **classify** (two reads, the register and the exchange): the exchange owes no further
  delivery (`mqttExchangeDeliveryDutyEnded`: ended, its delivery abandoned, or its
  generation discarded; all absorbing), the record retires; nothing of the allocation
  landed (exchange absent, the register absent or another allocation's, the attempt
  settled), the record retires and the withheld offer is NAKed, so the source re-offers
  it as a fresh delivery; landed, at `Publish`, the
  register this allocation's at `publish` with no token and not retired (W5b's
  population), the withdrawal is marked due and the record re-queued at once, so the
  withdrawal is the next unit's step; an indeterminate read, retained at its backoff.

**Every other state keeps the refusal, conservatively.** A possibly-attempted landing
(marker absent), one past PUBREC, one carrying an action token, or one
that cannot be read was NOT reached by any witness for this population, so no disposition
was built for it: the source's offers stay withheld (never doubled) and the record is
retried at its backoff. A same-generation resume whose recovery restores the
allocation's own entry supersedes the record: `trackPublish` then retires it and serves
the restored entry rather than refusing the offer, and the dispatcher's next unit retires
it too; this retirement is not route-witnessed (W5b's same-object-resume subtest
skips). Otherwise only a generation change drops the records, with the ledger. W5b,
with the record in place, observes the re-offer withheld, the first admission settled
and withdrawn on its standing marker, then the source re-offered and admitted once;
across a cold peer resume (`cold-peer-resume`), the peer's recovery withdraws the landed
never-sent obligation itself and at most one un-ended exchange exists throughout.

### A shared exchange depends on its exact acquisition

**Since 7a a shared-group QoS 1 delivery is an ordinary obligation.** It is admitted
through the authority (`admitSharedInflightPublish` -> `opAdmitPublish`) — register,
unsent marker and exchange in one batch — acquires its output, advances on its captured
acknowledgement, is charged by the custody ledger, and is withdrawn, abandoned and cleaned
up by the same continuations as any other exchange. The slot-only class
(`mqttDurIsSlotOnlyClass`) is the experimental affine route alone. Supported shared
delivery is QoS 1: a shared QoS 2 offer is diverted to the affine move before admission,
and the shared admission refuses any other QoS. `storeInflightRegister`'s sole remaining
production caller is that experimental route (chapter P converts it and deletes the
writer).

**What it depends on is an ACQUISITION, not a resource.** A group consumer is held by
several generations at once, so no per-generation resource can express it; what keeps it —
and with it the interest-retained source message a member still owes its client — alive is
that this generation's acquisition stays listed in its ledger (`shl.<idHash>.<gen>` on
`$MQTT_shared`). So the exchange carries `SharedAcq`, the exact `{Group, Inc, Acq}` it
depends on, written once by the admission and carried unchanged through every successor.
It is never re-derived later: a register can be destroyed without ending its exchange, and
a durable name identifies the incarnation, not which of this generation's acquisitions of
it the delivery arrived under (a multi-level filter's main and level-up memberships can
hold one incarnation through two). One pair rule, `mqttCheckSharedAcqPair`, binds a
register and its exchange wherever both are in hand — admission, action acquisition and
its write boundary, the acknowledgement class gate, abandonment, the withdraw door,
recovery classification and recovery owner selection: a register on a shared durable
requires an exchange naming exactly its incarnation's acquisition, any other register an
exchange naming none. A contradiction is an unsupported persisted shape: refused, never
inferred or repaired, and refused before any output.

**Which acquisition.** The delivery callback selects it once, under `sess.mu`, from the
session's own memberships (`sharedAcqForDeliveryLocked`): every Main or level-up
acquisition whose group key and incarnation match the delivery's durable and which has no
pending release verdict, the smallest acquisition nonce winning, so the choice depends
neither on map order nor on install order. It is captured with the SHARED tenure this
CONNECT acquires under and never recaptured on a ladder retry.  **Readiness is taken
inside the attempt, after the authority read.** `opAdmitPublish` reads the serving
authority, compares the connection's entitlement, and only then checks the shared
dependency (`mqttSharedAcqReadyForDependency`): the ledger valid and open, carrying the
captured shared tenure, listing exactly this acquisition; the group record serving this
incarnation and not retiring it; the physical consumer present. The batch CASes the
authority revision it read, so a readiness observation is fenced: an admission that
observed readiness before a later authority advance lands before it or loses its CAS, and
a retry re-runs the whole ordered check. Two tenures are compared and neither is merged:
the connection's entitlement against the authority's, and the captured shared tenure
against the ledger's (their consolidation is step 8's).

### The release fence: an acquisition is released only when nothing depends on it

**Why a release needs a fence (F-105 7e; designed at 7a, consult 82).** An unacknowledged
shared delivery is retransmitted by the group consumer RE-OFFERING its source — the register
holds only `Dur`/`Seq`, and the re-offer maps `(jsDur, sseq)` through `cpending` to the
existing identifier — and on the interest-retained `$MQTT_msgs` that source lives only while
some holder keeps the consumer. A release that ran L1 while an exchange still owed delivery
through that acquisition would, for the last holder, delete the consumer and the source with
it, leaving the exchange at `Publish`, its identifier and charge held, with nothing left to
send.

**One route.** Every release — UNSUBSCRIBE, forced leave, failed join, whole-packet rollback,
resume verdicts and cancellation (`executeOwnVerdicts`), the verdict sweep, T3 of a closing,
and the recovery executor's closing below — reaches L1 only through `executeSharedRelease`
(`shared_release_fence.go`). An OPEN ledger's release there runs, in order:

1. **CLOSE.** A ledger-only `close` batch adds the nonce to the ledger's `closed` list (any
   tenure composes it; its authority is the verdict executed). `closed` is monotone until
   the release removes the entry, and readiness refuses a closed acquisition
   (`mqttSharedAcqReadyForDependency`). The write boundary refuses a release from an open
   ledger whose prior does not list the nonce closed, and a release drops it from `closed`
   with the entry.
2. **FENCE THE AUTHORITY**, after a read showing the close durable. Atomic batches are per
   stream, so the close on `$MQTT_shared` and the admission's CAS on `$MQTT_inflight` cannot
   be one write; the ORDER is the fence. The authority is read at sequence S; if it is
   SERVING at the released generation a `fence-shared-release` transition (revision +1,
   nothing else, no member, SERVING predecessor) is committed against S. **Fenced means a
   CONFIRMED advance**: the batch landed, or a re-read shows a stored sequence past S — a
   committed write after the close, which every admission CASing S or earlier loses
   against. A rejection is not itself a fence (10164 says another batch is in process, not
   that one committed, and the in-process batch may be exactly the admission to exclude),
   so a non-landed outcome re-reads and an unchanged S re-attempts. Any other authority
   needs no write: RESERVING and PREPARING admit nothing and leave serving only by a write
   that moves the sequence, after which an admission reads the closed ledger; CLOSED or
   another generation never serves this one again (a generation is never re-proposed);
   ABSENT admits nothing (there is no missing-authority fallback); unreadable withholds.
3. **DEPENDANTS.** The generation's inventory is read after the fence
   (`mqttTraverseGenerationInventory`, the custody census's own traversal: the ledger's `Hi`,
   every duty 1..Hi, every exchange a duty names). The coverage rule puts every admitted
   obligation's duty in its admission batch, so every admission that landed before the fence
   is below that `Hi`, and none lands after it. An exchange naming EXACTLY this acquisition
   at phase `Publish` — the only phase that owes delivery from the source; a pending-drain
   phase owes an output drain, a delivery abandoned on an ACL deny hands its source back
   without awaiting the consumer, and the ended and discarded phases transmit nothing —
   WITHHOLDS the release (`errMQTTSharedReleaseWithheld`); any uncertain subject withholds
   as an error. Cost: O(Hi) per such episode, growing with the generation's history
   (F-112).
4. **L1**, and L2 for the last holder, as before.

**Two shortcuts, each an authorization rather than an observation.** A SEALED ledger
releases at once (step 4 alone): a seal is written only by a closing under a won teardown
claim or under the committed discarding closure, so the generation never serves again and
no retransmission of its is owed — a socket still attached while eviction catches up does
not restore a retired generation's entitlement. And where the generation's DISCARDING
closure stands, steps 2 and 3 are skipped: no admission or new output acquisition of it can
land (both need a serving authority at the generation), output already acquired is a drain
concern, and the 7d recovery owner ends every exchange. Neither shortcut waits on 7d's
progress, so the discard and the shared closing never wait on each other.

**A withheld release is re-attempted, never dropped.** The verdict stays in the record. The
verdict sweep retries it on every stable pass. And the OWNER re-triggers it
(`shared_verdict_kick.go`): when the session observes, for its current generation, an
exchange carrying a shared acquisition that has left `Publish`, and it owes a release, it
runs its verdicts again — from the STORED record only, because the in-memory map also holds
prospective verdicts between a membership removal and its save, and executing one would
close an acquisition the record still holds. The run is bound to the generation that kicked
it (the session object is reused across generations): it executes nothing unless the record
is still that generation's, drops settled nonces from memory only while the session still
is, and touches its kick state only while it still names that generation; a kick arriving
while a run executes sets `again`, and the run loops before it clears `running`.

**A denied shared delivery is handed back, never acknowledged.** Abandonment on an ACL
deny is durable exactly as for an ordinary delivery (the fact, the charge released, the
identifier kept), and the abandoned-ACK binding is installed as the MQTT acknowledgement
route. But acknowledging the source would consume the group's message on behalf of members
who ARE allowed it, so the source is never retired and never positively settled: the
disposal submits one paced NAK and settles. The class is closed at the primitive rather
than route by route: every positive source acknowledgement passes through ONE gate
(`submitSourceAck` / `submitSourceAckLocked`, `outbound_source_ack_gate.go`), which
refuses — submitting the paced NAK instead — while this session holds a HandBack for that
`{durable, sequence}`: a binding for it in the abandoned-ACK set, or a disposal owner
still unresolved. The check and the submission are one critical section under `sess.mu`; a
confirmed acknowledgement is prepared outside the lock, enqueued under it with the check,
and awaited outside it; a continuation's submission revalidates, in that section, that it
is still the installed owner; a hand-back is never a completion proof. A structural census
(`TestEverySourceAckIsGated`) fails on any positive-ack primitive, payload or request kind
named outside the gate. A re-offer of a held source to this member is handed back before
tracking, and a shared QoS 0 offer checks before output (a HandBack installed after that
check can overlap the write; the gate still hands back, and the resulting duplicate is
`docs/CONFORMANCE.md`'s stated residual).  **The HandBack lasts as long as the register.**
A SHARED binding is removed only through one boundary (`removeAbandonedAckBindingLocked`)
and only on proof that the exchange ended AND its register's deletion was positively
established (a confirmed identity-bound delete, or an absence read), or on the
generation's discard; an ending alone — which is all custody observation sees — keeps it,
so a re-offer is never acknowledged away while the register and the identifier it holds
still stand. An ordinary binding keeps its removal on the ending alone. Recovery
reconstructs a shared binding for an unanswered abandonment and for a Terminal exchange
still carrying the fact. A late PUBACK is routed by the binding and ends the exchange
Terminal; its cleanup settles the handed-back source by that ending alone, and the
register is deleted against it. For every binding, shared or ordinary, the one a terminal
cleanup removes is resolved from the set by the exact allocation
(`abandonedAckOfAllocationLocked`), never taken from what its terminal owner captured: a
PUBACK that captured the entry before the disposal installed the binding carries none. The
binding would then outlive the register, as a HandBack that hands back every re-offer or as
an identifier index that no later allocation on that identifier can install over.

**Close and resume.** The close's shared purge gives up only a shared delivery proven
never transmitted, through the ordinary withdraw door (a marker-evidenced tombstone and a
durable exchange ending; an exchange that cannot be read keeps its charge and identifier,
consult 32's ordinary disposition); a possibly-transmitted one keeps its identifier and
custody — a disconnect is not client completion — AND its source mapping. That last part
is the purge's SURVIVING-DISCONNECT mode (consult 85): the group durable survives the
disconnect and re-offers the source to this member when it resumes, so the mapping is what
makes that redelivery a retransmission of the SAME exchange under the SAME identifier with
DUP set ([MQTT-4.4.0-1]), on a resident resume exactly as on a cold one. A delivery-target
teardown (forced leave, deferred delete, shared release, UNSUBSCRIBE) still drops every
mapping. (The foreign-contest quarantine and its source-keyed decline are gone with 7b's
claim contest: nothing records a lost same-delivery contest any more.) What this does not
provide: if the group redelivers the source to
ANOTHER member while this one is away and that member acknowledges it, this member's
exchange stays at Publish, charged and reserved, until the generation is discarded
(`docs/CONFORMANCE.md`). A resume no longer CAS-claims shared (or any ordinary) registers:
7b replaced that contest with the inventory traversal and the connection's entitlement
(next sections but one).

### A restored delivery denied on resume is abandoned

An ordinary PUBLISH that may have been transmitted and is denied by the resuming
connection is abandoned durably. This remains a retransmission deviation.
Drain-claimed deliveries retain their separate drain-owned disposition and its
documented limitation; affine, retained, expiry, oversize, indeterminate authorization and
metadata-only destruction do not acquire this abandonment rule. A SHARED-group QoS 1 delivery
does since 7a — its abandonment is durable in the same batch — but its source is HANDED BACK
to the group rather than acknowledged (see "A shared exchange depends on its exact
acquisition").

The authority batch writes the exact register's abandonment projection and the
exchange's immutable historical fact together. The fact binds deciding tenure,
allocation, acquisition and source identity to a validated source ACK reply.
Creation requires the deciding serving authority and positive output evidence;
missing evidence does not prove that output never occurred. Every later exchange
rewrite preserves the fact. Charge reconstruction reads it independently of the
current phase, so later protocol advancement cannot recharge the exchange.

Local abandonment does not end identifier custody. An immutable ACK binding
survives scheduling-entry removal and is reconstructed from a validated pair.
Identity-bound PUBACK or failed PUBREC can end the exchange; successful PUBREC
establishes durable PUBREL intent, followed by canonical materialization, PUBREL
output and PUBCOMP. Live output actions retain their independent identifier hold.
Delayed completion compare-deletes only the captured allocation's binding and
cannot remove a successor's entry, source suppression or output hold.

A session-owned disposal contains immutable denial evidence, unresolved attempt
handles and exact allocation/source indexes. It is registered before worker
admission; admission refusal and failed shutdown attempts leave it owed.
Callbacks retain validated offers and wake this owner. AckWait and scheduling
entries are not its continuation owners. Off-lock completions and queued retries
check generation, allocation identity and installed instance. Ordinary recovery
cannot replace a busy disposal: classification leases the idle instance through
apply. A later successful resume installs its successor before releasing the old
restriction, obtains fresh authorization where needed, and persists the existing
transactional drain floor before activation. Local classification cannot complete
global recovery provenance or custody reconstruction.

Source settlement and MQTT protocol advancement are distinct. Ordinary registers
persist a validated SourceAckReply bound to their source; ACK-first Terminal or
Rejected successors retain this metadata even when abandonment never landed.
Their retained terminal register carries suppression and reconstructible source
cleanup, without inventing abandonment. Cold recovery does not need a source
re-offer or an in-memory reply. The source owner retains suppression through
confirmed settlement; submission or timeout alone is not confirmation.

The source-retention rule covers every live-generation deletion entrance:

- Recovery and reconciliation through `recoverPublishTerminalSlot`.
- `completeAcknowledgedPublish`, `attemptTerminalRegisterRelease` and
  `scheduleTerminalRegisterRelease`, including `resolveAckAttempt`, action-drain
  completion and shutdown final passes.
- `finalizeTerminalSlot` and `finalizeTerminalSlotObserved`, including correlated
  canonical/duplicate PUBREL disposal and continuation callers.
- `clearRetiredSource`, `resolveRetiredSource` and batched recovered-source cleanup.
- `deleteInflightRegisterFor`, including release, rollback and delivery cleanup.
- `deleteInflightRegisters`, `deleteInflightRegistersClassified`, collected
  recovery deletions, reconciliation and orphan cleanup.
- `reapObservedRegister`, `reapLoadedRegister`,
  `reapRegisterWithVerdictGated` and `reapRegisterGatedOutcome`.
- `reapRegisterWithVerdict`, `deleteInflightRegister` and
  `deleteInflightRegisterConfirmed`, reached only with an exact validated decision.  The
  common destruction-admission boundary independently requires source completion for
  ordinary terminal carriers, including no-fact carriers. Caller checks and collected
  sequences cannot substitute for this proof. The ONE exception is a shared terminal
  carrier whose exchange reads Terminal with its abandonment fact: its source was handed
  back and no completion can exist, so the boundary accepts a separately typed
  `mqttHandBackTerminalProof` — minted from a fresh exact-pair read and bound to the
  observed register version — in place of the source completion, and every other guard
  still applies. `reapIncarnationRegisters` and `deleteInflightRegistersPipelined` retain
  only the positively authorized generation-discard exception. Changed tenure or failed
  recovery is not discard authority. A live PUBREL action independently prevents terminal
  finalization; source completion does not drain that action.

Successful-PUBREC resolution has its own admission-refusal and shutdown owner;
a disposal owner does not own packet-derived PUBREC meaning. Failed final
attempts remain owed. After process loss, an unpersisted PUBREC cannot be
reconstructed from an abandoned pair, and an unlanded denial is not durable
evidence. Recovery reconstructs the durable branch actually present.

With stable serving authority and eventually successful operations, installed
owners converge without incidental traffic while their required actions remain
authorized. Failed or incomplete recovery that displaced an unlanded denial may
remain fail-closed until a later successful resume. Returning storage alone does
not authorize the old denial under a successor tenure. Exchange obligations,
unresolved handles and restrictions survive that window.

Generation discard uses the production close, drain, retirement-permit and
teardown path. It removes old ACK bindings and disposal/source indexes; queued
intent resolvers discharge upon observing retirement. Generation-scoped teardown
and its durable retirement evidence own surviving cleanup. Live output holds
survive reset until their holder drains; detaching a connection alone is not
generation discard.

**Acquisition history.** A register-only replacement now carries the occupant's `Acq` (the
composer) and the write boundary requires it: a continued obligation keeps its
transmission history. Before, the counter restarted at 0, which hid the last acquisition
from every reader and would have re-used an ordinal whose action record already exists.
The affine ladder writes its own replacement without that check (chapter P).

### The acknowledgement's phase is derived from the packet

Checking that a proposed phase is a LEGAL move from where the exchange stands is a real
check and a different property: a fabricated phase can be perfectly legal and still answer
the wrong protocol event. A PUBACK read as a PUBREC records a transfer of ownership the
client never made.

So the phase is derived from what a dispatch site actually has — the packet type, the
exchange's QoS read from its own record, and the reason code — and the resolution takes the
ARRIVAL rather than a phase. The packet carries no QoS, so the PAIR is what makes a
mismatch detectable, and a mismatch is an answer to a different obligation rather than a
badly-placed move. A refused PUBREC transfers nothing and owes no PUBREL. A PUBCOMP ends
the exchange whatever its reason code, because the only failure permitted there says the
client no longer holds it. An ending observed while this broker may still emit is the
PENDING-DRAIN variant, and that pairing lives with the derivation for the same reason
everything else here does.

### Destruction is authorized by the resource

A resource **names** the obligations depending on it, by exchange nonce, and the transition
authorizing its deletion CASes the resource record — against the very transitions that would
add a dependency. Winning that CAS establishes both that nothing depended on it and that
nothing can be added afterwards. **A live resource with no dependents is deliberately not
deletable**: nothing has excluded a dependency arriving between the read and the act,
and that
exclusion is the whole content of the authorization. Cleanup records a classified
outcome —
removed, gone or replaced — because a successful delete is not a completed cleanup.

**A COUNT WAS NOT ENOUGH, and the difference is the authorization itself.** A count can be
decremented by a transition that ended nothing: "one fewer" is an assertion, so a caller
stepping it down one at a time reaches zero with every obligation still outstanding and then
authorizes deleting the PUBREL consumer whose interest-retained records are those obligations'
only PUBREC evidence. A named edge is DERIVED at both ends — it is added only by the admission
that creates its exchange in the same batch, and removed only against that exchange's durable
TERMINAL phase — and it is removable exactly once, because the second attempt names something
the list no longer holds. For the source-replay and canonical-PUBREL roles the release rides
the very batch that ENDS the obligation (F-105 7c-lc), so it is never a later act and never
beside an authorization. A retained-material edge is released once its exchange can no
longer replay - ended, carrying the retained abandonment fact, or its generation closed
with Discard - as `mqttCheckResourceStep` checks.

An empty list is written as `[]` and never `null`: a null decodes to a nil slice that reads
identically to an empty one, and "this record says nothing about its dependents" would become
indistinguishable from "nothing depends on it".

### A dependency edge names a ROLE, not just an obligation

An edge is `(exchange nonce, role)`, and the role is the part that makes releasing one
safe. Three roles, closed: `source-replay` (the resource is required for permitted
replay), `canonical-pubrel` (it carries the release obligation; OWED and STORED are
states of this one role, not two roles) and `retained-material` (a retained exchange
needs its payload's material to replay its PUBLISH, 7c). Each is written by exactly one
admission route - the ordinary and shared admission takes the source consumer in
`source-replay` and, for QoS 2, the PUBREL consumer in `canonical-pubrel`
(`assembleAdmitDeps`); a retained materialization takes its owner resource in
`retained-material` - and each is discharged by its exchange's durable ending.

The reason is not tidiness. One exchange can need one resource for several reasons, and
with one edge for all of them, that edge's release has to stand for all of them. What
the boundary checks is `mqttExchangePhaseEnded`, and **Terminal means protocol
completion with no outstanding output**. For each of the three roles that IS the whole
proof - an exchange at Terminal has nothing left to replay and owes no release - so
`mqttRoleDischarge` maps every one of them to the exchange's ending. Its default arm
still fails CLOSED: a role whose discharge is not the exchange's ending would be not
releasable, costing reclamation and never an obligation. Decoding already refuses
every role outside the closed set, so that arm is unreachable today.

Every supported role is ONE aggregate need for the (exchange, resource) pair, so no edge
names a constituent: an edge carrying a `Ref` is refused, and the member is kept only so
that it can be, since without it the decoder would drop the key silently and read the
former shape as an accepted `(nonce, role)` edge.

**Four former roles are refused, not migrated.** `output-action`, `ack-handler`,
`source-settlement` and `shared-affine` were defined, with discharge evidence this
broker never recorded, and no supported route ever wrote an edge in one. Under the
compatibility boundary a persisted edge carrying one is an unsupported shape: it meets
the same "unsupported role" refusal as any unknown string (`mqttValidateResourceEdge`,
reached through `mqttDecodeOutboundResource`). There is no migration and no
reinterpretation. The refusal never licenses dropping an edge or deleting a resource: a
refused resource record is counted unreadable by the enumeration that meets it, is a
load error to `loadOutboundResource`, and the write boundary refuses any transition
that mutates it, so the resource and every edge it names stay exactly where they stood.

### Provisioning is a separate axis from retirement

A resource record is written BEFORE the durable it stands for is confirmed to exist:
`opProvisionResource` commits the record so an admission has something to depend on, and
the physical create is a separate act whose outcome may be unknown. So a resource can
legitimately be LIVE with its provisioning still in flight.

Authorizing deletion in that window is how an orphan is made — the delete finds nothing,
the delayed create lands afterwards, and the account carries a durable that no record
names and no sweep will attribute. `LIVE -> DELETE_AUTHORIZED` therefore requires
provisioning SEALED as well as a zero dependency list. Sealing is a positive fact and is
never inferred from a lookup that found nothing. A source or PUBREL consumer is the
exception: its create is unfenceable, so it is never sealed, and its authorization instead
requires a route's disposal decision and retires its physical name in the same batch — a
late create then lands under a RETIRED name nothing can adopt (F-105 §5.1, 7c-lc).

### The duty inventory: how work becomes discoverable

Enumerating records by subject filter is not discovery, for three reasons. It finds
RECORDS and not DUTIES — a provisioning operation or a cleanup has no record of its own
until it materializes, and a duty discoverable only once it has done its work is not
discoverable at all. It has no stable order, so a cursor over it must be a JetStream
sequence, and a sequence MOVES when a record is updated. And closure must seal a BOUND,
which a subject enumeration does not have.

So a generation carries a **ledger** (lifecycle state and an inventory high-water) and one
**duty entry** per obligation, provisioning operation and cleanup duty, at a stable ordinal
carried in the SUBJECT — the record's sequence moves and its name does not.

Allocation is a CAS on the ledger inside the admission's own atomic batch, which is what makes
ordinals contiguous: a batch that loses lands nothing, so no ordinal is consumed by a refused
transition and there is no hole a cursor can mistake for the end.

**Every duty is predeclared when the thing it concerns is admitted.** After closure the
inventory's SHAPE is fixed and only the states of its entries move. A resource's admission
reserves BOTH its provisioning and its cleanup duty, because the cleanup becomes
actionable when the last dependent goes — possibly long after closure, when allocating an
ordinal is exactly what the seal forbids.

**The seal is a fence, not a scan.** Closing a generation rewrites no exchange. The only
operation it must forbid is ordinal allocation, and allocation is the only operation that
CASes the ledger.

**An entry is never individually deleted.** A resolved duty is updated to its classified
terminal result and left standing; entries go only when the generation's root retires.
That is what makes "a missing or malformed entry is an inconsistency, not completed work"
coherent — absence is never legitimate, so it is never ambiguous between "done" and
"lost".

**A duty's ending is proved, not asserted.** Reaching TERMINAL requires the thing the duty
is about to have ended: an exchange at a durable ending, a resource with provisioning
sealed, a cleanup with its classified outcome recorded. Immutability of a terminal entry
preserves an ending; it says nothing about whether the ending was earned.

### Resume restores from the inventory, and ownership is the entitlement's (F-105 7b)

**One root per question.** A resume used to root every ordinary continuation in the REGISTER
enumeration and the PUBREL scan, beside a second, independent subject census of the same
exchanges for custody. After 7b:

| question | root |
|---|---|
| which ordinary obligations exist, and their custody (charge, identifier) | the generation's **duty inventory**: the ledger's `Hi`, read after the accepted CONNECT's finalize, then every duty entry `1..Hi` at its exact address (batched), TERMINAL entries included, then the exchange each exchange duty names (`traverseGenerationInventory`, for the resume and the background reconstruction alike) |
| which identifiers are occupied | the **register enumeration**, still: it is the only superset that covers affine, unreadable, illegal-shape and terminal-not-yet-deleted occupants |
| slot-only (experimental affine) continuation | the PUBREL scan, still; an ordinary PUBREL record authorizes nothing by itself |

A duty entry that is missing, unreadable or undecodable below `Hi` is UNCERTAIN by its own
address (the custody ledger holds a charge and withholds allocation until an individual
re-read decodes it); a re-read that finds a resource duty discharges the custody
uncertainty and concludes nothing about the resource. An absent ledger is an empty
inventory: it is created inside the first allocation's own batch and nothing deletes a
live generation's ledger. With a complete census an ordinary register whose exchange the
inventory did not reach is refused — its identifier reserved, nothing acting on it —
because restoration never manufactures admission; a pure cancellation tombstone is exempt,
being the cancellation fact itself. **Cost, measured, not a bound:** a resume reads every
ordinal the generation ever allocated, so its read count grows with the generation's whole
history, not with what is outstanding. With `Hi` = 5,000 (almost all terminal) the
traversal issued 5,000 duty reads in batches of 1,024 on the test server
(`TestF105ResumeInventoryReadsEveryOrdinal`, 2026-09-30); the accumulation of a long-lived
generation is the F-112 residual in `docs/CONFORMANCE.md`.

**Ownership is the connection's entitlement, and the register claim decides nothing.** The
property, applied to every ordinary mutation: > A mutation is **owner-dependent** when its
justification requires this connection's right to > decide for the session; it compares
the connection's captured accepted entitlement with the > serving authority INSIDE the
committing authority batch. A mutation justified entirely by > evidence bound to the
existing exchange or action is **owner-independent**: it keeps that > evidence's fences
(identity, phase, token, transmission, sequence) and never requires the > originating
tenure to still serve. An exact sequence or an unsent marker is not, alone, an >
authorization to cancel.

| class | operations |
|---|---|
| owner-dependent | admission and replacement; action acquisition; abandonment of a denied delivery; a withdrawal the connection chose (`opWithdrawUnsent`, under a LICENCE: the deciding connection's entitlement — the zero licence authorizes nothing, and an unlicensed withdrawal never falls back to a destruction); a cancellation tombstone without whole-exchange evidence (`tombstone-register`, `opTombstoneRegister`: the untokened publish occupant with `Cancelled` set, or a create-only tombstone for an allocation whose store is in flight); the disconnect and teardown void, which reaches the register only through those two; a canonical re-bind (`rebind-canonical`, below); the advance that must precede deleting a serving-generation pending fence (`fence-pending-disposal`, F-119) |
| owner-independent | the captured acknowledgement's advance (an old connection's PUBACK completes under its successor's standing authority, bound to exchange, slot, phase arrow and `Acq`); exact-token drains; the evidence-backed PUBREC re-phase; the proven-finished terminal advance and terminal cleanup; reaping a proven cancelled or complete occupant; the ordinary retirement mark (it records a successful-PUBREC suppression) |

Every owner-dependent call carries the licence of the connection WHOSE DECISION it
executes — `c.outboundEntitlement()`, immutable per connection — never a freshly read or
current one. The normal close passes the closing connection's (its `sess.c` is already
cleared by then); the parked close carries it in `mqttDeferredDisconnect.lic`. The
register's `Claim`/`ClaimSeq` stay written and structurally validated (dropping them would
be a schema refusal), and no ordinary ownership, admission, takeover or cancellation
decision reads them: the resume's claim contest, `transferCustodyForAdmission`'s ordinary
use, the ordinary `CustodyOnly` arm, the ordinary acquisition's claim equality and the
admission ladder's foreign-claim arms are deleted; the experimental slot-only class keeps
its claim machinery (chapter P).

**The sole current-binding exception (F-119).** The licence `runExclusionReclaim` captures
under `sess.mu` from the session's current connection and passes to
`reclaimPendingFenceStep` — and nowhere else — is not a deciding connection's: reclaim
makes a FRESH decision to dispose of a positively identified pending fence; it neither
replays the exclusion installer's cancellation decision nor ends an obligation. For a
serving-generation fence that disposal requires the quiescence proof over this same
session object's generation-matching custody ledger, then a confirmed authority advance
whose predecessor matches the captured connection's accepted generation and tenure; the
predecessor CAS fences a concurrent displacement. The proof covers every held admission of
the fence's nonce whose ladder has not returned, including admissions retained across a
resident rebind and resume reconstruction; an admission's retries keep their original
connection's entitlement, and a nonce is never restarted. The advance excludes attempts
already prepared, the proof excludes further attempts by the represented serving tenure,
and the entitlement compare excludes every other tenure. A missing or displaced
entitlement, a generation-mismatched ledger or a failed proof keeps the fence for retry,
and a captured licence is never refreshed inside the advance; a fence of a generation the
stored authority no longer serves takes the separate no-advance branch. This exception
authorizes no other use of the current binding's licence, and the licence census matches
it by its exact shape.

**The nonce verdict is the third durable representation of a cancellation.** Across
session objects it is arbitrated by the session record CAS (every save carries a record
transaction, and a successor's accept batch rewrites the record). Within ONE object the
verdict map is shared, and a later save marshals it, so a new verdict is staged only
through `stageCancellationVerdictLocked`, which requires the deciding licence to be the
object's `boundEnt` — the entitlement of the connection most recently ACCEPTED on it, set
beside the accept loop's `setOutboundEntitlement`, kept across a normal detach, replaced
by the next accept. A refused staging is the caller's no-verdict arm. Replay of an
already-durable verdict (record hydration, a fork merge) is not a decision and does not
pass through it.

**Displacement is observed durably.** The resume reads the client authority right after
the custody reconstruction and again immediately before apply, and refuses the CONNECT
when the serving tenure is not this connection's; apply re-checks the local binding
(`sess.c == c`) under its lock. A read is not a lock: a takeover after the second read
cannot make any owner-dependent write of the walk land, and it displaces this connection,
whose teardown discards what it installed. The walk's pre-apply session mutations are
owner-independent or unwind on refusal; the drain register observations are computed
before apply and installed only by it.

**An ordinary projection that recovery installs is a view over custody.** Invariant: an
ordinary pending projection the resume installs, retains or reactivates exists only while
the custody ledger holds its lineage. Install and release both run under `sess.mu`, so for
any pair one precedes the other. The recovery gate (`ordinaryProjectionHeldLocked`) takes
the VALIDATED register (never a lineage string) and refuses an unheld lineage, whatever
kind the entry it would install has; it gates every recovery install and every
reactivation, the entry's evidence comes from its constructor, and a refusal installs
nothing (the identifier is the ledger's if it is held and nobody's if not; only a
lineage-less occupant — an unreadable record, or an ordinary register the inventory did
not reach — keeps an opaque reservation, which confers nothing). A resident "in-memory
wins" keep needs no check of its own: a same-object resume keeps the held ledger entries,
and every accepted ending removes its lineage's projections under the same lock. **An
undecided inventory is not an ended exchange.** When the resume's inventory could not
decide a lineage's membership — the traversal failed, a duty ordinal was unreadable (which
names no lineage), or that lineage's own exchange is uncertain — a validated,
non-tombstone ordinary register seeds a PROVISIONAL held entry on its identifier before
the gate runs (`recoveryRestoreRefusedLocked`). The register proves its one-batch
admission landed; the holder creates no admission, overrides no complete inventory (one
without the lineage took the unpaired refusal) and authorizes no transmission by itself.
It keeps the delivery and its source mapping, so a redelivery returns the original
identifier rather than admitting a second exchange for one source, and it makes the
lineage an observation target: a live read adopts it without a second charge, an ended
read releases it with its projections. An ending accepted while any resume is in flight
vetoes the seeding (`endedDuringResume`, emptied when the last resume ends), so a resume
that captured the register before its ending never recreates a holder after the release.
`acceptExchangeObservationLocked` is the one place a decoded exchange observation is
applied — census merge, target observation, uncertain re-read — and the ledger there
reports the LINEAGES it released (independently of any charge: an abandoned exchange's
charge went long before its ending); every projection of a released lineage is REMOVED,
with the `cpending` mappings it owns. An accepted ENDED observation releases an existing
holder even from a census. Nothing removes a projection on an absence, on a charge-only
release, or by packet identifier. A durable ending not yet observed here leaves the
lineage held; the capacity and identifier gates request a re-observation pass when they
withhold, and that pass observes it. The LIVE paths that promote an entry to actionable
ordinary work — the placeholder-to-PUBREL promotion 7b left open among them — are closed
by the next checkpoint: see "A pending entry's authority is its kind".

**A vanished canonical PUBREL is re-materialised.** An ordinary `pubrel_ready` slot whose
named record point-reads absent while its exchange, read afterwards, still stands at
PubRecObserved (a PUBCOMP ends the exchange before any record disposal) is enrolled by the
resume in a continuation (`outbound_pubrel_rematerialize.go`) — for the SLOT, whether the
pass installs its PUBREL entry, finds one resident (a same-object reconnect) or finds the
scan's placeholder (a crash after a candidate was published, before its rebind). The named
record is "present" only at the slot's exact canonical sequence: an identity match elsewhere
is a non-canonical duplicate. The slot is never re-phased
— `pubrel_intended` is no arm a PUBCOMP accepts — so a PUBCOMP completes it at any moment.
Each attempt re-derives everything: eligibility (the PUBREL resource LIVE, ready for use,
carrying this exchange's canonical-pubrel edge, whose discharge needs the exchange's
ending, so the resource cannot be deletion-authorized while a rebind can land; otherwise
withheld, and no consumer is created); a new record published with an empty message ID and
proven by readback; a `rebind-canonical` batch under the recovering connection's
entitlement moving only the slot's canonical sequence; and settlement through the attempt
handle, a rejected rebind disposing of its candidate only after proving the register does
not name it. A ready PUBREL acquisition carries the canonical sequence its delivered
record was validated against and refuses a base that names another, so a callback for the
old record cannot acquire against a re-bound slot; the intended-to-ready direct arrow
still installs its tuple.

### A pending entry's authority is its kind (F-105 pending-entry structural closure)

**The defect this closes.** An entry in `pendingPublish` or `pendingPubRel` decided
whether it could act — be transmitted, NAKed at resume, admitted, enrolled in a drain, or
settle its source — from a conjunction of reservation flags that about ninety selectors
read, entries changed class IN PLACE, and the lineage was a field some writers filled and
others did not. The concrete instance: a resume's PUBREL scan leaves a lineage-less
placeholder; the acquisitions and the delivery callback wrote the acquired slot onto
whatever PUBREL entry was resident, and `trackAsPubRel` carried the lineage only from that
resident, so the delivered entry was an acquired, sendable PUBREL with no lineage. When
the exchange then completed on another broker and the ending was accepted here, the
lineage release could not match it: the entry, its mapping, its identifier and its Receive
Maximum charge survived for the life of the connection.

**The property.** Every entry has a KIND, and the kind decides what it may do:

- **Hold** (the zero value) occupies an identifier and authorizes nothing. Its sub-state
  is the reservation flags (`regPending`, `regCancelled`, `regForeign`, `markerOpaque`,
  the recovery provenance flags, `terminalReconcile`), which no other kind carries.
- **Ordinary** is an ordinary exchange's projection, and exists only while the custody
  ledger holds its lineage in this generation.
- **Retained** is a retained send's exchange (no register), and **Affine** a
  slot-only-class exchange (chapter P), classified so neither is mistaken for the others.

Which obligation an entry stands for is its EVIDENCE (`mqttPendingEvidence`: generation,
lineage, exchange nonce), produced by exactly three functions from a fact the caller holds
— a validated register, a landed admission, an acquired action — never from a caller's
string, and otherwise copied only from another entry's evidence in a constructor (a
successor of the same exchange) or from an abandoned-ACK binding (built from its record).
A Hold may carry evidence too: a reservation over a named exchange.

**Construction, promotion and the one writer** (`outbound_pending_kind.go`). Kind and
evidence are assigned only by constructors; a promotion builds a NEW entry and replaces
the old one, so holders of the old pointer (`h.entry`, an intent resolution's placeholder)
fail their identity comparison closed. Both maps are written by one function,
`setPendingLocked`, whose every call states its EXPECTATION at the identifier — empty,
exactly a pointer the caller captured where it decided the replacement was eligible, or
ANY at two recorded sites (the PUBREL callback's commit, which validated the resident
itself under the same lock, and the rollback reinsertions, which put back the exact entry
their caller removed). A mismatch leaves the resident exactly as it was; callers commit
what goes with an entry (its mapping, the F-093 handoff, an exclusion adoption) only after
it succeeds. For every expectation the writer refuses an Ordinary entry unless custody
holds its obligation (`ordinaryHeldLocked`): the ledger holds its lineage, or — for an
admission whose attempt landed behind a lost response and which the reconciler has not yet
adopted as the exchange — still holds the allocation's OWN admission, provided no ending
of a lineage that admission's attempts carry was accepted (`holdsAdmission`,
`endAdmissionsFor`); such an ending, accepted after the install, is reported released like
a holder's, so the projection the admission licensed goes with it. 7b's recovery gate
still gates every recovered ordinary-class record before its install, whatever kind the
entry has. Install and release both run under `sess.mu`, so either order is safe.

**The release.** An accepted ending takes the DELIVERY-phase entries carrying the released
lineage's evidence — actionable projections, allocations, the landed marker-opaque Hold,
placeholders — and not the TERMINAL-phase ones, whose job is to hold the identifier
through the slot's cleanup, which the ending precedes: a terminal reservation ends
nonce-keyed (`releaseTerminalReservation`, the reconcile continuation), never by lineage.
A delivered Ordinary PUBREL whose PUBCOMP this connection still owes (F-089's wire debt)
is not removed but CONVERTED to a released delivery (`mqttNewReleasedDelivery`): a Hold
that acts for nothing — no transmission, no resume NAK, no drain — keeping the ACK
subject, the slot binding, the evidence and the ledger charge, so the PUBCOMP handler
(deliberately not kind-controlled) still settles the slot through it and Receive Maximum
reopens at once. Its lifetime is its connection's: once that owner is no longer live by
F-089's predicate (the bound connection, or one a two-phase retirement is still
detaching), `retireReleasedDeliveriesLocked` — run at every allocation and at every bind —
retires it, handing a slot cleanup the completion worker still owns to the worker's
terminal reservation and otherwise removing the entry with its mapping; each retirement
replaces exactly the entry it examined, and a PUBCOMP whose captured entry was retired
meanwhile removes nothing.

**The action path.** An acquired PUBREL action becomes an entry in one place,
`bindActionToPubRelLocked`, which validates before it mutates anything: the resident
PUBREL entry is absent or carries the action's nonce, the resident PUBLISH entry passes
the F-093 handoff's ownership test, and the action is one the session may act on — an
ordinary action while custody holds its lineage, an affine one (no exchange, no custody)
in this generation. Only then is the entry built from the ACTION's evidence and slot and
committed with its mapping and the handoff. A refusal changes nothing; the drain armed at
admission gives the action back and AckWait re-offers the record. The acquisitions create
no entry; they refresh only the PHASE (sequence, state, acquisition, action fields) of a
resident whose captured slot names the same subject and nonce, which is the freshness
fence a later terminal delete is checked against. The PUBREC route's phase advance
likewise rewrites only an entry carrying its own slot's nonce. At write entry the callback
re-checks that the entry still ACTS for the exchange (Ordinary or Affine of the action's
nonce; exactly Retained for a slot-less retained exchange).

**Terminal conversions.** A PUBCOMP converts the delivered entry it completes into its
terminal reservation in the handler's own critical section (`pubCompConvertLocked`): the
entry captured after the lock is re-taken, its latest ACK subject returned for
acknowledgement, its exact mapping removed, its evidence and ledger charge kept, no ACK
subject carried; a registerless Retained exchange is simply untracked. The recovery and
reconcile installer keeps its contract: a fresh reservation into an empty identifier (it
names only the slot nonce and is released nonce-keyed, never by lineage), a replacement of
this exchange's resident that carries no delivery ACK subject, a refusal otherwise.

**Marker-opaque reservations.** The conversion of an allocation whose marker could not be
read classifies first (an affine allocation keeps HEAD's reservation, no custody
condition). An ordinary LANDED conversion requires custody to hold the admission's own
lineage. An ordinary OCCUPANT conversion (a withheld same-delivery replacement) stands
over a lineage the ledger did not hold at allocation (the allocator never hands out an
