(and the resume repair's) keeps the handle of every attempt it submitted. On exhaustion
each is resolved — LANDED or SUPERSEDED means it committed, NEVER_LANDED that its abort
won — and an unresolved one is ABORTED on its create-only outcome subject, after which it
can never land. An absent ownership is never the verdict: a queued claim can land after
any negative read. A landed claim's incarnation is disposed of like any other.

**The drain carries its decision's entitlement.** The entitlement of the connection whose
transaction set the removal mark is stored on the drain beside the mark, cleared with it
on a definite failure, and travels through the landed continuation and the queued disposal
(`{durable, entitlement}`), so a disposal executed after the transaction releases — with
no client — is still recorded under the decision's entitlement and never under the one
serving now.

**The sweeps.** The plain orphan sweep deletes only a RETIRED name's consumer: the
backstop for a delayed CREATE that resurrects a retired name after its cleanup completed
(a `CleanupComplete` records an attempt, not permanent absence). The QoS 2 sweep's PUBREL
arm now takes a RETIRED ownership as its whole licence; the F-036 retirement watermark it
required first was a single-slot record a later generation overwrites, so a resurrected
retired name could never be reclaimed once a later generation retired and a restart lost
the proof cache, and it never added anything (a non-RETIRED name is not deleted there).
Its pass-scoped memo is deleted with it.

**Readiness checks the consumer's effective configuration.** Beside the stream's limit,
the looked-up consumer's own `InactiveThreshold` must be zero; a consumer an administrator
armed is refused for new obligations. A snapshot, not a fence: see the supported-
configuration boundary in `docs/CONFORMANCE.md`.

**The PUBREL consumer's stable name is sanctioned same-owner rematerialization** (consult
110). §5.1's "a replacement uses a fresh name" governs a replacement OWNER: the canonical
PUBREL consumer's name is generation-scoped, and recreating a verified-absent consumer
under it while its ownership stays LIVE for the same incarnation is the legal `LIVE(o) ->
LIVE(o)`. A RETIRED name is still never reclaimed, and recreation recovers no PUBREL
records already lost with the consumer. The ensure refuses when the session's generation
and the serving authority's differ, so the name and its owner are one generation, and (since
7f) unless the resource the LIVE name owns is a LIVE, undecided PUBREL consumer; an enrolled
re-materialisation continuation calls it to recreate a consumer verified absent (see "A
serving generation settles its displaced tenures").

**What 7c-lc does not do.** Restart completion of an item the live owner did not finish
— the owner not resident, a crash — and the retirement of a generation's consumers at
its teardown were left to the recovery executor, and since 7d it performs both for a
DISCARDED generation (next section): a resource WITH a disposal decision is retired from
its record, and one WITHOUT one is given the closure-licensed `generation-discarded`
decision. A resource WITHOUT a decision in a generation that still SERVES — its route
crashed or lost its entitlement before the decision landed — is indistinguishable by its
own record from a serving consumer; its evidence is the successor tenure's accept, which
fences the displaced tenure's claims and saves, and the next accepted tenure decides it
(F-105 7f, "A serving generation settles its displaced tenures"). So 7c-lc is the mechanism
and the foreground SOURCE routes; 7d adds the discarded generation's half and 7f the serving
one's.

### A discarded generation retires through its recovery owner (F-105 7d)

A teardown closes its generation DISCARDING before it releases the session record, and
from that moment no connection of the generation exists to decide anything. Until 7d the
teardown then deleted the source, drain and PUBREL consumers raw and wrote nothing about
them, so their resources stood `LIVE` with `LIVE` names and hold edges for ever: no
Disposal could be written after the closure, the executor skipped their cleanup duties,
the generation's root rolled without end, and a late CREATE of one of those names was
never reaped (both orphan sweeps take only a RETIRED name). No exchange of the discarded
generation ever ended either.

**The licence is the closure.** `mqttGenClosure` is create-only and its `Discard` member
is immutable, written by the act that ended the generation (the teardown receipt's
close, or `opFinalizeHandoff`). Every act below that has no entitlement to act under is
checked at the WRITE BOUNDARY against the member's own generation's closure
(`requireDiscardingClosure`): a positive answer cannot become false between the read and
the write, so there is no window to arbitrate; an absent, unreadable or preserving
closure licenses nothing. A bare CLOSED authority, or a successor's entitlement, is
never the licence.

**`Discarded` releases holds and ends the duty; it is not an ending.** A new phase,
reached only by the new `discard-exchange` kind from a phase that has not released its
holds (`Publish`, `PubRecObserved`, either pending drain, `DeliveryAbandoned` — its
abandonment fact preserved), with every hold released in the same batch. An obligation
that already ended keeps its own ending and is never rewritten. The hold rules read a
predicate of their own, `mqttExchangeReleasesHolds`, and `mqttExchangePhaseEnded` —
which decides identifier exclusivity, custody, completion and the abandoned-ACK binding
— does NOT include it: a discard releases the Receive Maximum charge on the authorized
discard ground, but it manufactures no output drain and no handler discharge, so no
identifier, acquired action or captured binding of the original connection is released
by it. Identifier exclusivity is per generation and a discarded one admits nothing, so
nothing is held against anyone.

**The disposal decision of a discarded generation's consumers** is
`generation-discarded`, the one reason no route takes: recorded by the retirement,
licensed by the closure, carrying no tenure (the closed schema makes the tenure
reason-specific). A decision a route already recorded while the generation served — a
drain's `drain-retired` — is the one carried and is never re-requested.

**One executor, and a census that makes it complete.** For a root whose generation's
closure discards (read once per visit), the recovery executor classifies:

| Entry | Work |
|---|---|
| obligation that has not released its holds | `discard-exchange` |
| obligation that released them, its `rel` or own register standing | delete them, the `rel` first |
| source / PUBREL consumer, no decision | the `generation-discarded` decision |
| decided, still held | withheld: its holders are ended through their own duties |
| decided, nothing holds it | authorize deletion, which retires the name |
| deletion authorized | delete, classify, record the outcome and end the duty |

A delivery duty may already be RESOLVED while its obligation still owes discard work —
an abandoned delivery's resolves while it holds, a shared one holds nothing, an ended
retained one may still have its `rel` — so for a discarded root the sweep also returns
resolved exchange duties as CENSUS entries, and the visit counts one as unresolved
exactly while its work remains. No terminal duty is reopened and nothing is allocated
after the seal; the census only decides which ordinals the root may certify past. It is
complete because the boundary admits no obligation without a duty entry naming it in its
own generation. The census reads are charged inside the entry's own unit
(`mqttRecoveryMinimumUnit`, 16), so a visit always classifies at least one entry, and
EVERY early exit — budget or shutdown — truncates the cursor before the first entry it
did not classify. The `rel` goes before the register because the register carries the
`rel`'s identity proof; the teardown's register reap therefore spares a discarding
generation's retained registers. A PUBREL consumer is disposed of only once an enrolled
affine consumer's readiness — its PUBREC proofs secured — stands. An ambiguous physical
delete records nothing and is repeated: the name is RETIRED, so a repeat cannot reach a
successor (this closed row 6's "continuation 4").

**The prompt drive is a caller, not a mechanism.** The teardown kicks the root as soon
as its discarding closure stands — before, and independently of, the shared closing —
and a worker visits it with the pass's own `visitRecoveryRoot`: at most 32 visits per
kick, 8 per FIFO turn, a bounded set whose overflow is dropped. It judges no progress;
whatever it leaves is the periodic pass's, which promises eventual visitation and no
latency bound.

**Teardown transfers rather than deletes.** `classifyTeardownGeneration`'s DISCARDING
class now hands the source, drain and PUBREL consumers to the executor exactly as it
already handed the affine one; the PUBREC proofs are still secured first. A named
durable no resource of the generation names is left standing and reported. The VACUOUS
class (no closure, no ledger) and a teardown with no persisted record keep the direct
delete: nothing was admitted or provisioned through the authority there, so no
obligation holds those names and no ownership names them. The owner `destroy`, the
adopted teardown and the Clean-Start predecessor cleanup no longer wait on any of it.

**The release gate's root arm needs the discard.** A reachable root is durable recovery
ownership only where an implemented executor owns what it leads to — a discarding closure.
A generation closed PRESERVING its obligations has no executor for its delivery, release or
drain, so where its sealed inventory holds anything it must certify before its record goes;
an EMPTY sealed inventory has no surviving work for anyone to own, so its root suffices —
the abandoned reservation, the one preserving closure production writes. A currently
withheld supported step does not refuse.

**The discarded generation's shared closing is the recovery owner's (7e).** The clean-start
HANDOFF never ran a shared closing: its finalization writes the discarding closure, shared
groups are not enrolled, and the displaced record carries no verdicts, so the predecessor's
acquisitions stayed listed and their incarnations held for ever. The recovery executor now
runs the closing (seal, then every listed acquisition's sealed release, then the
`sealed && acqs == []` check) for every discarding-closure root it visits, licensed by that
closure, and **a discarded root certifies only when its shared ledger reads sealed and
empty** — never on absence, which an installation or a join could still turn into an open
ledger; the closing writes the seal over absence itself. The step runs only after a
sweeping visit's duty execution and cursor persistence, or at the certify point after the
roll decision, so its failure gates certification and nothing else; every dispatch is
priced at its full bounded cost (seal and release retry loops, the commit's prior re-reads,
the consumer delete and retirement loop) and at most four release episodes run per visit.
The inline closing on the two teardown routes stays — it also serves a receiptless teardown,
which has no root — and the two converge on the seal and release CASes.

**What 7d does not do.** A live generation's undecided consumer is **7f** (next section).
Exchanges, duties, resources and closures are still never physically deleted (F-112).

### One tenure and one closing driver (F-105 8b)

**One tenure per acceptance.** The outbound authority's tenure and the shared ledger's
tenure were two values minted independently; they are now one. The authority tenure is a
nonce the accept drive mints before any batch exists, so it cannot carry a sequence; the
ledger's order cannot be the session record's sequence either (`adoptResolvedMetadata`
reads the record's CURRENT sequence, which a later save may have advanced). So the
tenure is `{id: the authority tenure the acceptance was finalized under, seq: the stream
sequence of the acceptance's own fact}`. The fact is committed in the same atomic batch
as the record, create-only under a subject unique to the attempt;
`adoptCommittedMetadata` — the one adoption point of a live acknowledgement and of a
resolved commit — records which fact that was, and `mintAcceptanceTenure` reads it back
by subject and digest. Anything but the landed fact refuses the CONNECT. Installation
then runs on EVERY acceptance before CONNACK: installed or already standing activates;
superseded, sealed or unresolved refuses through the ordinary refusal path, which
certifies the connection closed (8a). A refusal after the authority is SERVING under the
tenure leaves the record and the authority standing, which is the next acceptance's to
settle; the ledger is untouched, because nothing but an installation creates one.

**One closing driver.** `destroy` and `finishAdoptedTeardown` run the receipted
discarding close (owner: the fast path from the discard boundary's load; adopter: from
the receipt) and then `closeRetiringGeneration`. T3's releases skip the release fence,
so the driver seals only where nothing can depend on an acquisition T3 releases — a
dependant needs an admission, and an admission needs the authority SERVING at the
generation (consult 122):

| state read (closure first, then ledger) | the driver |
|---|---|
| ledger already `sealed` | resumes T3 and T4: every production seal was licensed when written |
| a DISCARDING closure of the generation stands | seals, releases the SEALED set, T4 |
| admission fenced — a closure of the generation stands, or the generation NEVER SERVED (the authority read absent, or serving or closed at another generation, with no closure of this one) — AND the ledger absent or listing nothing | seals, releases the sealed set, T4 |
| anything else: SERVING with no receipt, a standing proposal, a preserving closure over a listed acquisition, an indeterminate read | WITHHOLDS: the record stays MARKED, its release is withheld |

A join landing after the driver's observation can be depended on by nothing; the seal
preserves it and T3 releases it from the sealed set, never from a snapshot taken before the
seal.

**Every adoption settles, and a receiptless one continues.** `finishAdoptedTeardown`
first runs the settle-only run the discard boundary uses (bounded by one request
timeout): a proposal standing over a marked record can only be aborted — its metadata
commit CASes the record at a sequence the marker claimed past — so settlement cancels a
preparation back to its serving predecessor or closes an aborted reservation. Expiry and
the orphan sweep have no CONNECT ahead of them, and without this a receipted close meets
PREPARING and refuses forever. A marker with NO receipt over an authority that, settled,
still serves its generation (the discard boundary's residue, an orphan-sweep re-claim)
is continued, not stranded: the adopter authors the receipt in ONE atomic batch whose
commit member is the marker itself, re-written byte-identical and CAS'd at the sequence
the adoption read it at (`claimTeardownReceipt`) — the receipt file's own rule, since a
receipt written after merely observing a marker authorizes nothing. Exactly one of that
batch and any other write to the record lands; a displaced marker supersedes the
adoption and no receipt is written; an unresolved outcome is classified by the receipt
(create-only, landing only inside such a batch), never by the marker's nonce, which
predates the batch. Such a receipt names the retired record's write identity but the
marker's own pre-batch sequence, since the retired record's sequence is not recoverable
from the marker.

**P2: the displaced record names the handoff's retirement targets, and a clean start
never discards behind an unresolved boundary.** A clean start decides ONCE, before the
retirement detaches anything, from the discard boundary's carried load (consult 123),
and the decision defaults to refusing with the incumbent intact. No record: the discard
arm. An authority not read, indeterminate or malformed, or a standing RESERVING or
PREPARING proposal at any generation: refuse — a preparation can cancel back to SERVING
at this very generation, and a discard there would mark the record from memory for an
adopter to continue into a receipt. ABSENT, CLOSED at any generation, or SERVING at
another: the discard arm, since no receipt can ever be authored for this generation.
SERVING at this object's generation: the record is proven at the object's exact
sequence, write identity and generation, and the handoff takes the affine and PUBREL
targets the finalization's discarding closure enrols from THAT record, never from
memory; a record gone or moved past the sequence takes the discard arm, whose claim is
superseded and re-drives against the record that won; no write identity, an unreadable
record, or an undecodable or foreign one at the sequence refuses. The metadata batch's
CAS at the proven sequence is what makes the record read the displaced one. Every OTHER
discard — disconnect, expiry, gone-retirement, the pending-discard finisher — marks from
the owning incarnation's own state, which is its to snapshot, unsaved resources
included.

**The close fast path never recomposes while an attempt is unresolved.** A close whose send
failed is resolved; never-landed recomposes; landed or superseded is done; anything else is
aborted and resolved again, and an attempt still not decisive returns the error (the record
stays marked, the adopter repeats) rather than composing a second close beside it — on the
owner's fast path and in the full episode alike (`settleCloseAttempt`). `destroy` no longer
takes a `discardAuth` flag: every discard takes the same receipt rule.

### A closure certificate outlives its process (F-105 8c)

A register's live output token (`ActionToken`) is the one production fact that says an
acquisition may still emit, and only its holder clears it: by its own drain once the write
returns, or paired with the terminal advance in `pubrel_terminal`. A holder whose drain
could not land retries in process; a holder whose PROCESS is gone — a crash between the
certificate and the drain, or before an unresolved drain was retried — leaves the token
standing for ever, and with it the identifier, its Receive Maximum charge and every
successor's acquisition. The process that owned the connection had already established,
positively, that the connection could never emit again. 8c makes that fact durable and
lets it end the token.

**The record.** `$MQTT.inflight.f105.cert.<idHash>.<gen>.<run>.<conn>` on
`$MQTT_inflight`, body `{id, epoch, gen, run, conn}`: which connection of which broker
run, serving which client generation, can emit nothing more. The connection token is
MINTED per connection, with the server-local number only as a prefix: one process may
construct several servers, each numbering its connections from one, and two sockets
sharing a name would let one's certificate end the other's tokens. A connection acquires
under exactly one generation — its entitlement is set once and refused on replacement — so
the generation scopes it without ambiguity. It is its own class, neither an arbitration
record nor an obligation: a fact about a socket that arbitrates nothing (two certifiers
write one fact), it is never a member of an authority transition, and no class enumerator
matches it. Written create-only and once: an answer that the subject is taken is settled
by reading back the identical certificate. It is never deleted within the recovery epoch,
like closures and outcomes; generation naming is not a reclamation path.

**Eligibility before the batch, persistence off the caller's path.** An acquisition
registers its connection's certificate context — the client generation, captured once —
BEFORE its batch is sent (`registerAcquisition` in `opAcquireAction`), so an acquisition
whose answer is lost still has its connection's certificate persisted. Whoever records the
certificate (`completeCertification`, reached by the torn writer and by the external
certifier alike) starts the one persistence attempt when a context stands; a connection
certified BEFORE it registers persists at registration. A connection that never attempted
an acquisition — a refused CONNECT, a subscribe-only client — persists nothing: it can
have left no token. The write runs in its own goroutine with only the captured context, so
no certifier waits a store round trip or takes a lock to state a fact it already
established (the torn writer certifies under the delivery's lock). One attempt, no loop; a
failure is logged and leaves the in-process certificate valid.

**The clearance, and its licence.** `clearCertifiedActionToken` ends one register's token
when, and only when, all of these are proven from durable state: the register is ordinary
(a slot-only register has no action record) and carries a token; the action record at the
register's own (lineage, transmission counter) decodes as this client, epoch and
generation, carries the register's identifier, and is of a kind whose token can stand in
the register's state (a PUBLISH token survives a successful PUBREC into `pubrel_intended`
or, retained, `pubrel_ready`; a PUBREL token stands in `pubrel_ready` and
`pubrel_terminal`); a durable certificate names exactly that action's connection; and the
write lands at exactly the sequence the register was read at. Never a rebase: a register
that moved may carry a successor's acquisition, so the whole licence is proven again from
a fresh read. The write is the register with its token, claim and claim sequence cleared
and NOTHING else — not the phase, the transmission counter or the unsent marker. The
certificate proves no further output; it does not say the frame was unsent, so it never
withdraws, never abandons and never releases an identifier: whether the next transmission
is a DUP is decided from the transmitted fact as always. In `pubrel_terminal` the token is
the only thing keeping the exchange pending-drain, so the clearance is the paired drain
completion — token clear and terminal advance in one batch. A write whose answer was lost
is recognized by the identical body it leaves (the holder's own drain writes exactly that
body), and adopted at the sequence it stands at.

**Where it runs.** A resume clears every certified token of its generation BEFORE its
register walk (`clearCertifiedTokensForResume`), gated on a complete listing of the
generation's certificates — none, or a listing that could not be completed, licenses
nothing. The walk then classifies authoritative state unchanged: nothing is reloaded
inside it and no reclassification is spent. A landed clearance moves a resident entry that
still references the exact pre-clearance sequence onto the landed one, as the holder's own
drain write-back does; an entry another writer moved keeps its fact. A PUBLISH or PUBREL
acquisition that meets a standing token runs the same clearance once before it refuses,
and re-proves everything from a fresh read if it lands; a token nothing meets in between
stands until the next resume. Every other gate that refuses on a token is unchanged.

**Deleted with it: the whole-exchange discharge proof.** `proveExchangeDischarged`, the
connection's local drain oracle and `mqttActionDrained` had no production caller: they
stated a second definition of "may still emit" beside the token that every gate reads. 8c
gives the certificate one consumer, the token, and deleted the second definition rather
than wiring it.

### A serving generation settles its displaced tenures (F-105 7f)

A persistent session's generation keeps SERVING across every resume: each accepted CONNECT
mints a fresh **tenure** for the same generation, and only a session end discards it (7d).
Every route that ends a subscription records its decision under its own entitlement and hands
it to the session-resident retirement owner, whose custody is in memory. A crash, a takeover,
or an entitlement that moved before the decision landed therefore left a source consumer LIVE
and undecided for the generation's life, and a decided one whose retirement was unfinished
stood decided but never retired: the recovery pass never visits a serving generation (its
licence is a closure), and the plain orphan sweep deletes only RETIRED names.

**The licence is the successor's accept.** Once tenure T' of generation G is accepted, the
displaced tenure T can write neither a session record (the accept advanced the record's
sequence, and every save CASes it) nor a claim (every provisioning CASes the authority at
exactly T). So "provisioned under a tenure that no longer serves, AND named by nothing the
serving tenure holds" is a fact no later write by T can falsify. This is what the withdrawn
7c-lc rule — "no record names it" — lacked: under the SAME tenure a later save can still
name the consumer after the read (a multi-filter SUBSCRIBE provisions a plain consumer and
names it only in its final membership update).

**The provisioning tenure is on the record.** A source or PUBREL resource carries
`prov_tenure`, the tenure whose claim created it: required on those two kinds and absent on
every other, proved equal to the displaced SERVING authority's tenure by the creation
boundary (a hand-built batch cannot stamp a foreign one), and immutable. A stored source or
PUBREL resource without it is an unsupported shape and is refused.

**Two new decisions, both a source consumer's only.** `tenure-superseded` is a successor's
decision about a consumer a displaced tenure provisioned: the write boundary admits it only
when the resource's provisioning tenure differs from the deciding one, beside the existing
rule that the deciding entitlement is the one serving. `repair-replaced` is the resume
repair's decision about the durable it replaced. Neither may decide a PUBREL consumer. What
the boundary does NOT prove is the naming half — the session record is on another stream
and no batch carries it — so that half is the settlement's, read under a record
transaction.

**The settlement.** At the end of every accepted RESUME, after the resume reconcile, a
background job of the resident session walks the generation's resource records — a paged
stream-info subject listing that follows the offset until it reaches the total the answering
page reported, duplicates ignored (resource records are never removed, F-112, so between two
pages the sorted set only gains entries and an insertion re-reads one rather than skipping
one) — and classifies each SOURCE resource once:

- decided (`Disposal` stands) and LIVE or DELETE_AUTHORIZED: handed to the retirement owner,
  whose step finds the decision standing and continues from the state that stands;
- undecided, LIVE, provisioned under another tenure, and named by no subscription, drain or
  retained adoption of the session (read under a record transaction, so no route is
  mid-transaction): handed with `tenure-superseded` under this connection's entitlement;
- otherwise (named, this tenure's own claim, CLEANUP_COMPLETE) nothing.

The PUBREL consumer is never settled: it is one stable name per generation, never in Cons
or Drains, reused by the successor's ensure. An unreadable listing or resource leaves the
visit incomplete and the job retries with capped backoff while the session is resident and
its tenure still serves; residency loss, server shutdown or a FINALIZED displacement ends
it, and the next accepted tenure runs its own. A handoff merely PREPARING over this tenure
is not a displacement — a cancelled one restores exactly this tenure, and no successor would
then exist to settle what was abandoned — so the job carries on and the retirement owner
WITHHOLDS a disposal that meets the preparation rather than dropping it; it lands once a
cancellation restores the tenure, and is dropped to the successor once a finalization moves
it. Nothing durable records the job. A held unnamed source is the 7a consult-85 residual (an
exchange stuck at `Publish`); the owner waits on its holds as for any route.

**The owner keys its work by tenure.** A source item's key carries the tenure its decision
is recorded under, so a displaced item still pending on a same-object resume can no longer
swallow the successor's: the displaced one fails on its moved entitlement and is dropped,
the successor's proceeds, in either order. Every step is an idempotent CAS against the
resource record, so two entries on one consumer cannot interleave destructively.

**The resume repair decides its predecessor.** When the reconcile replaces a vanished durable,
the replaced durable is handed off `repair-replaced` after the confirmed save, under the
connection's entitlement — the 7c-lc rule that every route ending a consumer records its own
decision. An unresolved save decides nothing; whichever record lands, the next tenure's
settlement finds an unnamed predecessor. Both the repair's claim and a SUBSCRIBE's claim are
now made under the CONNECTION's entitlement rather than the authority that happens to stand
when they read it, so a connection displaced between its gate and its claim never labels a
claim with its successor's tenure.

**Fork repair never reinstates a decided consumer.** A recognised fork's capsule is this
broker's own erased branch, and a consumer it names may since have been decided by another
broker's tenure (the survivor's settlement disposes of a consumer the survivor's record
does not name). Reinstated into the accepted record, such a consumer would need a
lifecycle of its own; it is kept out instead. Fork repair samples the outbound authority's
sequence FIRST, then reads, for every consumer of ours the merge would install, whether it
still serves (ownership LIVE for this generation, resource a LIVE source consumer with no
disposal); every read completes before anything is merged. A consumer that does not serve
is not reinstated — a membership keeps its grant without the consumer and the resume
reconcile provisions a fresh one; a drain is omitted (the residual in
`docs/CONFORMANCE.md`). An unanswerable read refuses the CONNECT before its accept, the
capsule kept. The accepting CONNECT's own handoff preparation then CASes exactly the
sampled sequence: a disposal writes the authority, so one landing after the reads refuses
the preparation with `errMQTTForkFenceMoved`, and the accept loop takes the FULL re-drive
— the merged object is discarded and fork repair reads again — never the inner retry,
which would re-drive the same merged state. After the preparation the authority is
PREPARING and a disposal is refused, so no decided consumer enters the accepted record by
fork repair. The expectation survives the preparation's internal re-attempts and is never
refreshed; a creation-arm accept carries none (with no authority no disposal exists).

**The PUBREL consumer is recreated inside an enrolled continuation.** The ensure now also
reads the resource its LIVE name owns and refuses unless it is a LIVE, undecided PUBREL
consumer. The 7b re-materialisation continuation, when its eligibility fails, repairs
exactly one cause: the consumer verified ABSENT under its standing LIVE ownership, with a
LIVE undecided resource and a stream whose inactivity limit cannot reap it (checked
independently — an absence says nothing about the stream). It clears the connection's
verification and calls the ensure, which recreates the consumer under the same owner (the
sanctioned same-owner rematerialization); the next attempt publishes and rebinds. An armed
threshold, a spent or foreign name, a decided resource and an indeterminate read stay
withheld. The promise is scoped to an ENROLLED continuation: a successful rebind ends it,
so a later loss is an operator deleting a broker-owned consumer, repaired at the next
resume.

### Boundaries and stated limits

What the converted broker does is stated in the status paragraph at the head of this
section and in the mechanism sections above. These are its boundaries:

- Acknowledgement processing tests `sess.c == c`: an acknowledgement arriving on a
  connection that is not the session's attached one is refused. One for an identifier
  with no pending entry is resolved only through an allocation's acknowledgement binding,
  a HandBack or an AckRoute (`resolveAbandonedAckLocked`), never by reading an occupant by
  identifier. Ordinary
  capacity and identifier custody belong to the exchange (row 5, the custody ledger), a
  shared-group QoS 1 one's too since 7a, a retained one's since 7c; experimental affine
  ones are still counted from the scheduling maps until chapter P converts them. An
  ordinary obligation destroyed as never transmitted WITH its marker evidence ends
  durably; without that evidence the door refuses the destruction (F-088), and an
  exchange that nothing can answer keeps its charge and identifier in the ledger until
  the generation is discarded (F-106's accepted cost, `docs/CONFORMANCE.md`).
- The durable directory IS populated and IS walked: every closure allocates a reachable
  root in the same batch, an account-manager pass visits them on the periodic sweep's
  cadence, and the executor performs the affine cleanup family end to end - authorize,
  delete, classify, complete and resolve - then retires the generation with a
  certificate. That affine executor is EXPERIMENTAL and its claim is CONDITIONAL on both
  premises stated above (F-107, now chapter P's, and F-108); the directory, the pass and
  the retirement machinery around it are supported infrastructure. An admission
  allocates its obligation's duty ordinal in its own batch, and a resume roots custody
  in that inventory (7b). Recovery still walks the in-flight registers by subject filter,
  as the occupant superset, and still scans the PUBREL records (`scanPubRelRecords`) for
  the canonical PUBREL: the inventory roots the restore and those walks complement it.
- The duty CONTINUATIONS classify what an outstanding duty owes, and a pass acts on
  exactly the
  verdicts named above. `deliver`, `release`, `drain` and `provision` are withheld by
  stated rules; in a DISCARDED generation none of them is owed, and the executor performs
  its retirement instead (7d, "A discarded generation retires through its recovery
  owner"). A SHARED group durable is no longer a duty of this authority at all: the
  shared-group lifecycle transfer (2026-09-22) gave it a group record, an acquisition
  ledger and incarnation-qualified names, and a shared closing is what frees it — the
  teardown's inline, or the recovery executor's for a discarded generation (7e) — so no
  generation carries a shared cleanup DUTY in its inventory; what holds a discarded root
  open is the certification condition that its shared ledger read sealed and empty.
- The metadata-release gate's inputs are a TRI-STATE whose zero value is UNKNOWN, and
  unknown WITHHOLDS release. The gate reads durable records, never the caller: the
  closure (which carries the discard disposition as a mandatory member, written by the
  transition that closes the generation), the inventory ledger, the reachability of the
  recovery root at the closure-recorded address, and the completion certificate
  (`gatherAdoptedReleaseFacts`). It is vacuous only for a generation with neither a
  ledger nor a closure, which admitted nothing. It reads no target enumeration: a
  source, drain or PUBREL durable of a discarding generation that no resource record
  names is left standing and reported (`reportUnenrolledTargets`), never deleted on a
  missing record. Production claims every such name before its CREATE, so it does not
  write that shape.
- Two MIXED emitter sites still reach the transport without passing either output
  boundary: the generic locked emitter `mqttEnqueueProtoLocked` (one raw write) and the
  raw branch of prepared PUBLISH delivery `mqttEnqueuePreparedPublishMsgTo` (two). They
  carry supported QoS 0 and actionless acknowledgements, and beside them the
  obligation-carrying traffic of experimental affine QoS 2 (chapter P's), which is why
  the cutover plan's EMPTY bypass set is not met and is not claimed. Every other emitter
  is on a boundary: CONNACK, the server, displacement and shutdown DISCONNECTs and the
  3.1.1 SUBACK write through `writeActionlessFrameBy`, which validates the bytes (a QoS
  1/2 PUBLISH, a PUBREL, a partial frame or a trailing packet is refused) and takes only
  `wmu`, so each emitter keeps its claim-and-write or write-and-record `c.mu` section
  whole; and any QoS 1/2 frame outside the slot-only class requires its acquisition and
  goes through `writeAuthorizedFrame`, refused rather than written raw without one. The
  structural check parses the package and refuses any raw transport write that is
  neither a boundary nor a recorded site, and
  `TestF105OutputBypassSetIsTheTwoMixedSites` requires the recorded set to EQUAL the two
  mixed sites by key and count. A count cannot say which traffic a site carries, so
  `TestF105SupportedObligationsNeverLeaveThroughAMixedSite` watches the frames at both
  sites across live delivery, retransmission, retained replay, shared delivery and the
  resends of a resumed session and a restarted server, and sees no QoS 1/2 PUBLISH and
  no PUBREL.
- Material REMOVAL is enforced in two places with a gap between them. The announcement —
  the purged count, the closure requirement and the exact-resource authorization — is
  enforced in the transactional validator, so no batch escapes it. That nothing is
  DELETED before the announcement lands is enforced only by `purgeMaterialStep`, because
  a JetStream delete is its own call and the validator never sees one. Since 7c a raw
  `deleteMsg` on `$MQTT_inflight` outside the named removal functions —
  `deleteChunkInterval`, `finishMaterialRemoval`, `disposeRetainedRel` and the register
  reapers — fails the untagged delete-route check; that check is structural, not a fence.

### Storage this mechanism accepts

Nothing deletes an authority, a transition outcome, a generation closure, a name
ownership, a closure or completion certificate, a resource, an exchange, an action, a
ledger, a duty, a directory shard or a readiness record during the account's recovery
epoch. The only
deletes on `$MQTT_inflight` are of registers, unsent markers, `rel` records, retained
material, recovery roots and a discarded obligation's records, each at an exact sequence.
There is no proof that every delayed caller has stopped referring to a permanent record,
and an expiry would rebuild the inference-from-absence the whole mechanism removes. So
storage grows with the activity accumulated in the epoch; there is no reclamation, and no
fixed ceiling is claimed.

What that means per event:

- **Permanent F-105 records are on `$MQTT_inflight` already by an account's first
  accepted CONNECT**, with no obligation admitted. The accept drive runs at least two
  authority transitions (reserve then finalize-creation, or prepare then
  finalize-handoff), each of which CASes the per-client authority and writes its own
  create-only outcome in the same batch: at least two authority writes and two distinct
  permanent outcomes per accepted CONNECT. The authority is one retained subject
  rewritten in place; the outcomes are new subjects, so write volume and retained
  subjects are different counts. A CONNECT that committed a reservation or a preparation
  and then failed can leave the same records behind.
- **Each admitted QoS 1/2 obligation** adds its exchange, its outcome and its dependency
  records (resource edges, the ledger and its duty entry), and each later authority
  transition on it, its acknowledgement advances among them, adds another outcome. A
  consumer name claim adds a permanent `own` record, and a certified connection close
  its certificate.
- **Retained delivery (7c) stores a COPY PER SUBSCRIBER**: each admitted retained QoS 1/2
  delivery has its own manifest and chunks, its owner resource and two duty entries, its
  register and marker, its exchange and actions, and for QoS 2 its `rel`. Concurrent
  obligations are bounded by capacity (Receive Maximum and the scheduling budget), and
  NOTHING bounds the total: copies whose exchanges ended wait for their reclamation, a
  failed materialization's material waits for the next CONNECT or closure, and repeated
  SUBSCRIBEs each take fresh copies. The owner resource records are kept at
  CleanupComplete.

**Exposure to the upstream data-layer defects** (`docs/known-upstream-issues.md`). This
states which live operation meets which defect; it does not reopen any upstream
prerequisite and adds no compensation.

- **MAXMSGSPER-REVIVAL** (a limit-evicted version revives at a store recovery; witnessed
  after a crash and, in a second witness, after a clean shutdown, with no cause
  inferred - see `docs/known-upstream-issues.md`). The
  permanent records above remove whole-stream emptiness as an escape for every account,
  single-session accounts included, from its first accepted CONNECT. They do not
  establish that a neighbour shares a register's storage block, and that placement is
  not claimed. A revival-eligible register exists only after an admission, and only
  where the ack advance's CAS rewrite (which limit-evicts the previous version), the
  survivor's explicit delete and a store recovery that brings the evicted version back
  all occur. The purged chunks and
  manifests of retained material, and a limit-evicted manifest version, are exposed the
  same way.
- **F-108** (a failed store read answers as the end of a suffix enumeration). The
  supported suffix enumerations are the next-message walks through
  `loadNextMsgFromSeq`: `scanPubRelRecordsCharged` (`unsub_drain.go:3227`), which every
  PUBREL scan reaches - resume recovery (`recoverInflightRegistersOnce`), drain recovery
  (`recoverDrainPubRels`), `findOwedPubRelRecord`, `disposeTerminalPubRelRecords`, and
  the teardown's proof walk (`secureQ2AffPubRelProofsCharged`, run on every teardown
  that holds a PUBREL durable); the orphan sweep (`adoptAbandonedTeardowns`,
  `orphan_qos2_sweep.go:557`; `condemnRetiredSurvivors`, `:667`; `buildSessionRefs`,
  `:860`; `collectInboundQoS2Candidates`, `:1229`; `collectInflightCandidates`,
  `:1659`); `sweepSessionExpiries` (`mqtt.go:8773`) and
  `sweepOrphanedConsumersBefore` (`mqtt.go:8942`); `scanWillOutbox`
  (`will_outbox.go:955`); the acceptance-fact walk `loadNextAcceptFact`
  (`sess_accept_fact.go:344`); and `sweepSharedGroupRetirements` and
  `sweepAcqReleaseVerdicts` (`shared_lifecycle_sweep.go:128`, `:168`). The two affine
  claim walks (`qos2_shared_affine.go:3820`, `:4008`) are chapter P's. The custody duty
  traversal (`traverseGenerationInventory`) is NOT a suffix enumeration: it reads named
  ordinals at exact subjects through `loadLastMsgForMulti`, bounded by the ledger, and
  an unreadable ordinal is uncertain by its subject. The `STREAM.INFO` subject listings
  (`streamSubjectsComplete`, `enumerateInflightSubjects`) are a different API and are
  not counted here.
- **F-109** (a point-read failure answers as absence). The CONNECT ownership reads
  (`loadOutboundAuthority` through `loadConnectOwnershipInput` and
  `standingProposalID`, and `resolveMetadataAttempt`) and the record loads every
  decision rests on: `servingAuthority`, `loadOutboundExchange`,
  `loadOutboundResource`, `loadNameOwnership`, `loadGenClosure`, `loadGenLedger` and
  `loadGenCompletionCert`.
- **F-110** (a create-only CAS is admitted over an unreadable occupant). Every
  transition's create-only outcome and closure, the first name-ownership claim, and the
  closure and completion certificates (`publishDurableCloseCert`,
  `publishGenCompletionCert`).

## Orphan reconciliation

A broker that dies in the wrong window leaves durable state nothing else ever
revisits: an inbound QoS 2 hold and its release claim on `$MQTT_qos2in`, a
assignment claim on
`$MQTT_qos2assign`, an orphaned `$MQTT_PUBREL_*` consumer, and the teardown marker that
pins them in place. A session-affine `$MQTT_Q2AFF_*` consumer on `$MQTT_out` accumulates
too and is deliberately **not** converged — see the affine subsection below. None of
them loses a message BY ACCUMULATING — a stalled claim is honored, never released (nor is
a stale `discarded` marker among them a counterexample any longer: it records the fence its
writer was entitled to destroy, so a later exchange above that fence reaps it and proceeds
— F-062 mechanism 2) — but all of them accumulate. A periodic per-account sweep converges
them
(`internal/mqtt/orphan_qos2_sweep.go`), beside the existing session-expiry and
orphaned-consumer sweeps.

**Shared group consumers are classified by their group record, and shared release
verdicts are executed on stable observation.** The orphaned-consumer sweep's record walk
still decides PLAIN durables by reference; for a `$MQTT_SHARED_` consumer it reads the
group record instead and classifies the consumer's ordinal — live (retain), retiring
(finish the delete and clear the entry), derived retired (delete: the delayed create that
landed after retirement), old shape without an ordinal or no readable group record
(retain, warn) — so no enumeration's exhaustion licenses a group deletion. A pass over the
group records finishes any `retiring` entry a leaver's crash left, and a pass of its own
over the session records executes the release verdicts they carry once the same verdicts
have been seen on two consecutive passes, connected or not, never
writing the record. Neither pass is an arm of the consumer sweep, whose "no candidates"
early exit must not suppress them. See "A group durable is held by arbitration, not counted
by a scan".

**Teardown markers are adopted first.** A marked record deliberately reads as a
reference to everything it names, so until it is finished none of that session's
QoS 2 state can become eligible. Once the marker has been *stably observed* for the
grace — keyed by the record's sequence and teardown nonce, so a resave or a peer's
teardown restarts the wait — the sweep re-reads it, requires that same sequence and
nonce, and runs `finishAdoptedTeardown`. No stored timestamp participates: neither
the record's store time nor `Teardown.StartedAt`. A young marker, an unreadable
record or a failed adoption leaves everything referenced.

**Then retired survivors are condemned.** The pass walks `$MQTT_teardown` — the
watermarks, one per client, bounded by the client-ID population — and for each valid
fence loads the client's record. An unmarked record carrying the retired generation is
the hollow survivor of the claim-won deletion window, and with no live winner and no
CONNECT this is the only reader left for it. Eligibility is a stable observation of
**both** identities, the record's sequence and the watermark's, so a resave, a peer's
teardown or a newer retirement restarts the wait; the record is then validated with
`mqttValidateTeardownTargets` and re-read at those exact sequences, and the sweep
writes a teardown claim.

It **marks only**, and the *finish* is left to the marker-adoption class on a later
pass. That ordering is deliberate: releasing the record in the same pass would remove
it moments after the marker landed, and a survivor broker whose lossy record watch
dropped that brief observation would face an absent record rather than a moved one —
which is the F-036 shape, where a bound Keep Alive 0 client strands. Deferring narrows
that route to the case where the survivor's committed-read backstop does not reach the
record in time; it does not close it, and a CONNECT that adopts the marker finishes
immediately by design (see `docs/findings/ha-arbitration.md#f-036`). Nothing here
reaps a watermark, so there is no reap step and no GC choice that could widen the
escape the fence covers.

**Every destructive arm additionally requires a RETIREMENT PROOF, and that is F-036 unit
2.** The walk below establishes that no record and no local resident names a generation.
It cannot distinguish that from a session live on ANOTHER broker whose record is absent —
a resume preserves the generation, so such a session still uses these very names — and
destroying its state is payload LOSS rather than leakage. So:

> Any arm of this pass that can still destroy live session-generation state requires a
> valid retirement watermark whose generation EQUALS the candidate's. Without that proof,
> RETAIN.

One arm meets this differently since F-105 7c-lc: the PUBREL consumer delete's licence is
the
name's RETIRED ownership, which is reached only through a deletion authorization — every
hold released, a route's disposal decision standing, the resource authorized in the same
batch. That is strictly stronger evidence that no live generation depends on the consumer
than the watermark, and unlike the watermark it is not a single slot a later generation's
retirement overwrites, so it alone licenses that delete.

Everything below is KEPT as well; the watermark is an ADDITIONAL licence and replaces
none of it. `mseq` gives no second dimension here — this pass holds no `sess.seq` for a
remote generation, and cross-stream sequence comparison is meaningless — so the proof is
exact generation equality alone. A valid MATCHING observation is remembered in a bounded
positive-only memo; losing it to a restart or the bound costs a cleanup OPPORTUNITY and
never a licence, which is what makes caching sound here and unsound for every negative
outcome. The memo holds ONE generation per client because the durable watermark does.

**Today's census of arms that mutate from this false-absence premise**, recorded as the
current enumeration rather than as a claim that it stays complete: the `discarded` claim
creation and the nonterminal hold purge in `reconcileOneInboundQoS2`; the
absent-generation register delete in `reconcileOrphanInflight`; the consumer delete in
`deleteOrphanPubRelConsumers` (keyed by `refs.pubRelDurables` and its own record re-read,
NOT by `refs.hasInbound`, so its gate sits at its own authorization point after the
durable-name parse, and is RETIRED ownership since 7c-lc); and `discardAbsentWinnerClaim`,
which is **deliberately UNGATED and
out of scope** — it is affine assignment mutation, and F-036's supported-scope ruling
accumulates affine-only regressions under ROADMAP chapter P instead. A structural
inventory guard over these was designed, reviewed three times and DELETED: a
primitive-only AST inventory cannot catch a new unsafe CALLER of an already-inventoried
destructive helper, and completing it needs the bounded SSA reachability this repository
has ruled disproportionate, so the guard could not honestly claim a fifth arm cannot
appear silently. The behavioral negatives with exact payload assertions, and their
positive controls, are what protect the property.

**What still runs WITHOUT proof is the non-destructive tail**, and it is what keeps the
gate from being a blanket retain. Once the payload is authoritatively ABSENT, removing the
fence that protected it destroys nothing: an unchanged exact-sequence claim is deleted
after the hold is proven gone, and a terminal `Nmqtt-Q2Done` tombstone is reaped — the
exchange it belongs to already delivered onward and committed, and the PUBREL branch that
answers from it answers identically from its absence. The tombstone's order is
exact-sequence CONFIRMED delete, then an authoritative absence read, then the claim
re-read at its exact sequence, then the claim delete; the absence read is the step that
licenses the claim removal, and the confirmation ahead of it is defence in depth that
reports the failure at its own site. The defensible claim about the claim delete is
narrow and stated as such: it cannot destroy a payload and cannot let a NEW releaser
verify the old hold as Held. It does not eliminate the pre-existing post-proof
paused-releaser residual, which stays exactly as `docs/CONFORMANCE.md` records it.

**A permanently retained population costs bounded REVALIDATION work — and that is a
narrower claim than bounded work, deliberately.** Retaining without limit would otherwise
make each pass pay a session-record read, a consumer lookup and an ownership read for every
retained candidate, forever, so that part of the pass's JetStream traffic would grow with
the accumulated leak and eventually monopolise the sweep goroutine — a cost accepting the
storage leak did not include. Two bounds answer that part, and neither weakens the
licence. The PUBREL candidate set is revalidated under a per-pass budget with a cursor
keyed by the durable NAME, so the bound is a rotation rather than a truncation: every
candidate is still revisited, just not on every pass. A name rather than an index is what
makes it survive churn — an index modulo the current length is shifted by every insertion
and deletion before it, so a sustained arrival-and-departure rate could otherwise keep one
candidate outside every window forever. The supported claim is eventual visitation of a
PERSISTENT candidate under a finite or serviceable churn rate, not fairness against
arrivals that permanently exceed the budget. (A pass-scoped memo of negative watermark
observations used to bound the PUBREL arm's proof reads; it went with the arm's watermark
gate in F-105 7c-lc, whose RETIRED-ownership licence the watermark only ever shadowed and
which a later generation's retirement could permanently mask.)

**What is NOT bounded, and is stated rather than implied:** the consumer LISTING, the
candidate collection and the sort still grow with the `$MQTT_out` population. That is this
sweep's pre-existing shape — `consumerList` already walks the whole population, including
the affine consumers the course-E leak accepted — so paging that shared enumeration is its
own roadmap item and not something this gate closes.

**The accepted price is a permanent, UNBOUNDED leak** in STORAGE, and it is preferred to a
loss —
the same trade course E already took. Because the watermark is a single slot per client, a
generation whose slot has since been replaced can never again be proven retired, so its
nonterminal holds (carrying full application payloads) and its absent-generation registers
are retained forever. (Its PUBREL consumers no longer are: since F-105 7c-lc the PUBREL arm's
licence is the name's RETIRED ownership alone, not this watermark, and since 7d a discarded
generation's PUBREL consumer is retired by the recovery executor, which retires its
name.) No bounded
variant exists from current facts: a dead generation with an absent record and a live
remote one with an absent record are observationally identical to this pass, and waiting
longer does not distinguish them. An exact bound would need permanent per-generation
retirement history — trading unbounded payload retention for unbounded metadata — or a
distributed liveness lease, with a substantially larger failure and partition model.
Stream limits and `MaxAge` are not a solution, because their bound is implemented by
deleting the acknowledged payload. Stated in `docs/CONFORMANCE.md`.

**Absence is established by a complete walk, never inferred from a partial one — and
that is a narrower claim than "proven".** Candidates are listed *before* a complete
walk of `$MQTT_sess`, so a resource created between the two is never judged
against a snapshot that predates it; local in-memory sessions count as references,
covering the create-before-save window on this broker. What the walk plus this broker's
residents cannot observe is a session live on **another** broker whose record is absent —
a resume preserves the generation, so such a session still uses these names. That is
**F-036**'s false-absence inference, and since unit 2 it is GATED rather than open: every
destructive arm of this pass additionally requires a valid retirement watermark naming the
candidate generation, and RETAINS without one (see the proof gate above; the PUBREL consumer
delete's licence is its RETIRED ownership instead). The
per-resource-class consequences belonged to F-034 — whose audit closed on 2026-08-22,
routing its own live-owner residue back to F-036 as that finding's fourth manifestation —
and to F-036, rather than to this section. What survives is not the inference but its
price: the accepted, unbounded retention leak in `docs/CONFORMANCE.md`.
(`$MQTT_qos2assign`'s class was F-033, whose
audit closed on 2026-08-18. What it found in this pass is one defect of ours — a live
generation reference makes this pass skip every claim of that generation, leaving them to
an
owner resume that may never come, which is F-064. (F-036 also gained an addition here —
the affine consumer delete was BY NAME and a resuming session ADOPTS the consumer it
finds, leaving the instance fingerprint unchanged so it discriminated nothing. That is
HISTORICAL: course E removed the delete, and the population it created is gone with it.)
**F-064's accumulation
half has since narrowed the skip**: under a live reference the pass now reaps claims that
are already durably TERMINAL, and collects the retired affine `$MQTT_inflight` register
class with the copy and claim each names. The skip still protects every NONTERMINAL claim
of a live generation, and that is a proof rather than caution — no fact such a pass could
write is both true and terminal for that population, and writing `Discarded` there makes
a concurrent materializer withdraw an unpublished copy for a session that never ended.
See the F-064 bullet in `docs/ROADMAP.md` for the worked interleaving.) The same
bound is stated once for
the code, in `internal/mqtt/orphan_qos2_sweep.go`'s header. Ownership is the
`(client-ID hash, generation)` pair carried in the subject or durable name, never
the hash alone. An incomplete walk, an undecodable record, a client ID that does
not hash back to its subject token, or an unvalidatable generation aborts the
whole destructive pass.

**Two grace policies, and neither is an age.** `mqttOrphanSweepGrace` (five
minutes) covers construction windows — a resource created just before the record
save that references it — and applies to teardown markers, holds, assignments and
PUBREL consumers. `mqttQoS2ReleaseOrphanGrace` (one hour) applies to release
claims, which arbitrate against a releaser that may be paused between loading a
payload and delivering it.

**Nothing subtracts two timestamps.** There is no clock to compare against: a
JetStream store time is assigned by whichever server led that stream's Raft group
at that instant, four streams are four groups, and one stream spans several clocks
across a leadership change — so a fast leader's timestamp minus a slow leader's
says nothing about elapsed time. Comparing either against the bridge's own
`time.Now()` is worse, for the reason the release claim's self-reported `At` was
rejected: the bridge is an external client on its own host.

So a grace is a **stable-observation requirement** measured on this process's
monotonic clock. A candidate becomes eligible only once it has been seen,
unchanged and authoritatively orphaned, across a monotonic span at least as long
as the grace — and **never on the pass that first saw it**: the first valid
observation only records the identity, and a later complete authoritative pass is
what may qualify it. Any identity change restarts the wait (a record's stream
sequence, a consumer's durable plus `Created`, a teardown nonce), as does the
resource becoming referenced again. Stored timestamps are diagnostic only. Failed
or incomplete scans record nothing and authorize nothing, and a mutation is still
revalidated at the moment it happens, separately from that eligibility check.

The observation table is bounded, and when it is full it **refuses new entries
rather than evicting**. Evicting is what a cache does and is exactly wrong here: a
deterministic scan revisits candidates in the same order, so admitting each new key
by evicting the one due next would make every sighting look like a first sighting
and nothing past the cap could ever qualify. Refusing keeps a stable resident
cohort that ages, is acted on, and releases its slot; entries nobody has revisited
in a very long time are pruned so a vanished resource cannot hold a slot forever.
State that is **retained by design** — a `Lost` assignment, or a `Discarded` one
whose source is not yet proven closed — is resolved before any observation and
holds no slot at all: it needs no wait, since it is already durably terminal, and
it is exactly what accumulates. Letting it occupy the table would let one account
fill it and refuse every other candidate permanently.

Two consequences, both erring towards leaving state alone: a broker that restarts
more often than the grace never reaps, because quarantine is in-memory and starts
over; and convergence takes several passes rather than one.

**The hold dies before its fence.** A `discarded` marker is reaped by nobody at
teardown time — it is the only durable proof that a late releaser must lose — and
the sweep may retire an aged one **only** after destroying the hold record and
confirming it gone. (A releaser reaps one only where it can prove the marker never fenced
its exchange; that condition and its evidence are F-062's.)
A releaser that preloaded the payload and resumes afterwards
then wins a fresh create-only claim against an empty subject, but its mandatory
authoritative re-read returns `mqttQoS2VerifyGone`, so it delivers nothing.
Reversing the two steps returns `mqttQoS2VerifyHeld` and fans the message out
again. An unclaimed hold is fenced by a fresh `discarded` marker before it is
purged, and every claim delete targets the exact sequence just read.

A record that cannot be *read* is still a fence — the claim write is a create-only
CAS, which fails while any record occupies the subject — so an aged unreadable
claim retires by the same route: purge behind it, then delete its exact sequence.
It is deliberately not deleted first and replaced with a fresh marker, because
that empties the subject while the payload is still there.

**One definition of an interpretable record, shared by every path that reads one.**
The reference walk fails closed on a record it cannot interpret, but the
post-snapshot re-reads are what actually authorize a mutation — so they apply the
same validation, not a subset of it. A record written after the walk whose client
ID does not hash back to its subject, whose generation is malformed, or whose
affine pair is inconsistent is **indeterminate**, never proof of absence: reading
it as "a valid record for a different generation" would discard a live assignment
or delete a referenced consumer along with its interest-retained copies.

**Every deletion target is validated against the record that names it.** A teardown
adoption deletes the `Cons`, `Drains`, `PubRel` and `Q2Aff` durables a marked record
carries, all copied verbatim, so a record naming another session's durable would
have that consumer deleted and its interest-retained messages with it. Each name is
bound to its session — a plain durable is `<idHash>_<nuid>`, the PUBREL and affine
ones are fully derived — and adoption checks all four. A **PUBREL** consumer is
additionally re-looked-up immediately before deletion and must still be the same
instance quarantine observed: one deleted and recreated under the same name is a
different consumer, and deleting it by name would destroy a peer's fresh consumer
inside the very create-before-save window the wait exists to protect. The affine
consumer had the same re-lookup, and it was not sufficient — an adoption preserves
`Created` — which is part of why course E removed that delete rather than hardening it.

**PUBREL durables are reaped, and they are the only consumer class this pass reclaims from
a CANDIDATE LISTING.** (Not the only affine-consumer delete reachable from a sweep pass:
teardown-marker adoption still reaches `deleteTeardownTargets`, as above.)
`sweepOrphanedConsumers` lists `$MQTT_msgs` only, this pass reclaims no affine consumer by
absence since course E, and the reference snapshot had no PUBREL class at all —
so a `$MQTT_PUBREL_<idHash>_<gen>` consumer created just before the record save that
names it (`ensurePubRelConsumerSubscription` provisions it first) was unreferenced
forever if its broker died in between, holding its interest-retained PUBRELs with it.
The class was built as the affine one's mirror, and now stands on its own: the durable is
parsed back to `(idHash, generation)`,
its config must match all three names that identity derives — durable, filter subject
and delivery subject — at discovery *and* again at the pre-delete lookup, since a
consumer that disagrees with its own name cannot be attributed at all. A record is a
reference through the `PubRel` durable it names verbatim, and a *local* session through
the name derived from its `(idHash, generation)` unconditionally, which is what covers
the create-before-save window on this broker. The class shares nothing with the affine
inventory and is deliberately not gated on it: an unreadable assignment claim suppresses
the affine CLAIM pass, and only that, because one persistent corrupt claim must not
disable PUBREL reclamation account-wide on evidence about a different resource class.
Deletion is authorized by a final
authoritative record re-read — a save landing after the reference walk aborts it, and
does not change `Created`, so the instance check alone could not catch it — and then by
re-looking-up the same instance. **What those checks cannot observe is a session live on
another broker whose record is absent** (see "What AUTHORITATIVE means" in
`orphan_qos2_sweep.go`): whether deletion in that state costs anything for this resource
class is not answered here, because it belongs to the finding that owns the class rather
than to this section. Deleting the consumer drops the PUBRELs it held, which
is correct in every state those checks can observe: no observable session could deliver
them and the identifiers died with the session. Both windows are narrowed rather than
closed, because a consumer delete is by name and unconditioned; that residual, and the
resume-side verify-and-recreate that bounds it, are in `docs/CONFORMANCE.md`.

**The affine side is not a mirror image: the sweep's candidate-reclamation route no longer
infers affine-consumer deletion from ABSENCE.** That is course E's invariant, and the
wording is deliberate — it is not "nothing reachable from the sweep deletes an affine
consumer", which would be false. The sweep adopts abandoned teardown markers and finishes
them, and `deleteTeardownTargets` deletes `t.q2AffDur`; see the structural guard below for
what that route is and is not licensed to claim. What was removed is the inference from
absence, and the reason is that no positive fact can authorize it: the retirement watermark
records the **session** generation (`recordGenRetirement` writes `Gen: t.gen`) while the
consumer is keyed by an **affine** generation that outlives incarnations, so
`refs.hasInbound(idHash, ps.Gen)` and `refs.hasAffine(idHash, ps.Q2AffGen)` are different
keys and neither licenses the other. Consumer metadata has the same mismatch;
`NumPending == 0` is an instantaneous observation rather than a fence; and a record
re-read cannot tell "no session" from "a live session whose record is absent", which is
F-036's own premise. `$MQTT_out` is interest-retained, so a wrong delete destroys
acknowledged QoS 2 payloads — and the guards that read as defenses were not: a resuming
session ADOPTS the consumer through a create-or-update, which leaves
`ConsumerInfo.Created` unchanged, so the instance fingerprint cannot see it.

Assignments are still reconciled: an absent winner's claim is committed `Discarded`, and
claims are deleted only through `reapQ2AffClaim`, whose predicate refuses a claim marked
`Lost` and requires **both** `SourceAcked` and the copy to be absent. That two-sided
requirement is what makes the removal a leak rather than a no-op: with the consumer
retained the copy stays present, so such a claim is revisited every pass and reaped only
once another authorized actor removes or acknowledges the copy — a completed delivery
after an adoption, `settleRetiredAffineRegister`, or a lifecycle deletion (teardown,
rollback, a successful unwind). The accepted price is stated in `docs/CONFORMANCE.md`:
an unbounded correlated leak of the consumer, its copies and those claims, with no
automatic backstop, since the affine consumer's `InactiveThreshold` is deliberately zero
and `$MQTT_out` refuses `ConsumerLimits.InactiveThreshold`.

**The acceptance condition is behavioral**:
`TestOrphanSweepDoesNotReclaimAnAffineConsumerByAbsence` drives the real pass through every
state that used to authorize the delete and asserts the consumer AND its exact retained
copies survive, so a reintroduction fails it whatever syntax carries it.

Beside it, `TestQ2AffineConsumerDeletesAreInventoried` is a **drift alarm and an enforced
licence inventory**. It holds an exact, multiplicity-checked inventory of every
`$MQTT_out` consumer delete **in the package** — five sites — each with the reason it is
allowed to exist, plus the one call that routes a delete through a stream-generic ephemeral
helper. It has no reachability phase: four successive review rounds each evaded the
reachability step rather than the inventory, so it was deleted. Anything uninventoried fails,
a duplicate fails, and a stream that cannot be resolved to a named constant, a delete taken
as a method value, or a package-level function literal all fail CLOSED.

**Its claim is bounded to match its reach**, and this is deliberate: it detects direct and
common-indirect reintroduction, and is **not** a soundness proof, because AST analysis cannot
resolve Go function values, interface dispatch or reflection. Making it sound would need
closed-world type-checked SSA, which is disproportionate for an alarm the behavioral test
above does not depend on.

Of the five inventoried sites, `deleteOrphanPubRelConsumers` judges only `$MQTT_PUBREL_*`;
`ensureQ2AffineConsumerSubscription` and `finishQ2AffineUnwind` are session-fenced lifecycle
routes whose failure has no retry anchor; and `deleteTeardownTargets` (both its PUBREL and
its affine durable) is reached through teardown-marker adoption, and is carried as a
**known pre-existing call site with no claim that it is race-free**: a won `claimTeardown`
authorizes proceeding with lifecycle teardown relative to the claimed record, but it does
not fence a stale same-affine-generation peer's `beginQ2AffOp` and create-only claim CAS,
so `discardQ2AffClaimsFor`'s scan can be outrun. It is outside course E's change and it is
**outside F-036's closure too**, deliberately: this is AFFINE state, and F-036's licence
names the SESSION generation while the affine one outlives incarnations, so no retirement
proof can gate it. Under F-036's supported-scope ruling that work is accumulated under
`docs/ROADMAP.md` chapter P rather than held against this finding, with F-063's
proof-to-ack residual behind its second half.

**Two abort-capable siblings carry every refusal this pass makes about a claim.**
`advanceQ2AffClaimChecked` and `reapQ2AffClaimChecked` take a caller-supplied precheck;
`advanceQ2AffClaim` and `reapQ2AffClaim` are thin wrappers passing nil, so their existing
callers are unaffected. The precheck runs on EVERY attempt, against the record that
attempt will actually CAS, after the load and the existing identity fences and **before
`next := *cur`, before `mutate`, and before `mergeProven`** — the only placement that
vetoes. Carrying the same condition inside `mutate` cannot veto at all: `mergeProven`
runs after it unconditionally, and on an `AffineDone ∧ Lost` record `mergeProven` clears
`Lost` by itself, so the CAS lands with the closure having mutated nothing, normalising
the very shape the condition existed to refuse. The checked reaper applies its precheck
at TWO points — its own initial load, and inside the conditional `SourceAcked` advance —
and deliberately not a third after that advance returns, because the precheck is an
invariant that transition preserves and a post-return call is not a fresh load.

`reapQ2AffClaimChecked` also returns a typed outcome, `reaped` / `retained` /
`indeterminate`, because a caller that deletes an in-flight register only once the claim
it references is provably gone cannot distinguish those three from a function that
returns nothing. An authoritatively absent claim and a not-found delete are both
`reaped`; a refused precheck is `indeterminate`, never `retained`, since a refusal proves
nothing about the record and must not license a dependent deletion.

**The retired affine register class is collected with its copy and its claim.** A live
record protects such a register through the INBOUND session key, a different key from the
claim's affine one, so it needs its own arm. `settleRetiredAffineRegister` acts on what
the register's own source proves — and for an affine delivery the source IS the copy.
Where that source is `Complete` the exchange is over and the triple is resolved; a
nonterminal claim of the same assignment there is a CONTRADICTION and everything is
retained rather than trusted to the record-before-ack ordering. Where the source is
`Live` and the message at the register's own sequence sits on the copy the register
names, the register is durable evidence of a successful PUBREC, which licenses recording
`AffineDone` — deleting the copy at its exact sequence with a CONFIRMED delete, reaping,
and deleting the register LAST because it is the only proof of that licence. `Unknown`
and `Lost` settle nothing: an unreadable source is not an absent one, and a knowably gone
consumer means the delivery was lost rather than finished.

No stream gains a `MaxAge`: JetStream age eviction cannot perform this ordering or
these cross-stream proofs, so protocol state stays explicitly reconciled (every
stream's startup validator now rejects a global `MaxAge` — see "Stream
prerequisites"). The
inbound walk is bounded per tick by both a record count and a byte budget (the
message-get API returns whole records, so scanning a hold transfers its payload),
with a cursor seeded pseudo-randomly once per process and advanced sequentially
from there — random so a restart loop does not rescan the same prefix forever,
sequential so coverage inside one process is linear. The cursor is scheduling
state only.

## JetStream domain

The broker is a plain client of exactly one external JetStream, so `-js-domain`
(`MQTTNB_JS_DOMAIN`) is the single source of truth. There are no leafnode or
per-account topologies to resolve between, unlike the NATS Server this code came
from. Empty -- the common case -- means the domain of the server the bridge is
connected to.

The value is used in two places that must agree:

- **JS API subjects.** Requests are rewritten from `$JS.API.<x>` to
  `$JS.<domain>.API.<x>`.
- **Session subjects.** Sessions are stored at
  `$MQTT.sess.<domain>.<client-id-hash>` in `$MQTT_sess`.

Because the domain is part of the session subject, **changing `-js-domain` on an
existing deployment orphans every existing session**: the records remain in the
stream under the old token and the broker looks for them under the new one.
Treat a domain change as a session reset, not a configuration tweak.

The same setting also drives the `internal/backend` JetStream client
(`jetstream.NewWithDomain`), so both paths address the same domain.

`-js-domain` must be a **single subject token**: no `.`, `*` or `>`, no
whitespace, no control characters. This is deliberately narrower than the NATS
Server, which rejects `.`, `*` and `>` but would accept a domain containing
invisible whitespace or control characters -- such a value looks right in config
and logs while silently producing a JS API prefix and a session namespace that
are not what anyone typed. Ordinary non-ASCII is accepted, so a legitimate
Unicode domain the server would take is not refused here. Invalid values fail at
startup rather than surfacing later as unroutable requests.

## Backend seams (see docs/PORTING.md)

| Concern            | Mechanism                                             |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| Sessions           | JetStream stream (last-msg-per-subject), keyed by CID |
| Retained messages  | JetStream stream + subject tree metadata              |
| QoS1/2 persistence | JetStream durable consumers                           |
| QoS0 routing       | NATS core pub/sub                                     |
| Asset management   | `mqttJSA` request/reply over the service `*nats.Conn` |
| Per-client authz   | Auth passthrough: one `*nats.Conn` per MQTT client, plus the identity snapshot taken on it at CONNECT. NATS enforces SUBSCRIBE admission and QoS 0; the broker enforces publication and service-owned delivery |

## Auth passthrough

On CONNECT, the MQTT username/password are used to dial a per-client
`*nats.Conn`, and the broker then asks that connection **who it is**:
`$SYS.REQ.USER.INFO` answers with the bound NATS account and the identity's
publish and subscribe permissions. That one request is what makes the rest of
this section possible. Without it the broker knew only that the credentials
authenticated, which is why publishing was unenforced, the account was unbound,
and a subscribe deny stopped at SUBSCRIBE admission.

The request is made twice: once on the service connection at startup, **before
the MQTT listener opens**, to learn the account the broker's own streams live
in; and once per CONNECT on the client's connection, inside
`isClientAuthorized`, before the CONNECT is accepted.

### The identity snapshot

What the answer yields is a **snapshot**, taken once and never refreshed:

- **the bound account**, compared for exact equality with the service account.
  A mismatch refuses the CONNECT. This is the v1 same-account constraint below,
  which until now nothing enforced.
- **the publish permissions**, which gate every MQTT-originated publication.
- **the subscribe permissions**, whose DENY side is evaluated per message on the
  service-owned delivery routes. The ALLOW side is not re-evaluated: NATS
  already applied it when it accepted the subscription.

**Every unknown refuses the CONNECT**, and the list is exhaustive rather than
illustrative: a request that times out or errors, an undecodable body, an API
error, an empty user, an empty or mismatched account, a permissions object
present but missing a direction, a permission entry that is not a valid subject
filter, or a reported expiry already elapsed. A malformed deny that merely
"matches nothing" would be a fail-open, so it is refused rather than compiled.

A permissions object that is **absent entirely** is the shape a server with no
ACLs configured emits, and it means unrestricted. That is the default
deployment, so reading it the other way would refuse every publish everywhere.

### The snapshot's validity is the connection's validity

A per-client connection reconnects indefinitely and re-authenticates each time,
potentially under changed permissions, so a snapshot outliving its connection
would authorize service-owned stores on behalf of an identity that no longer
holds. The broker therefore installs a disconnect and a closed handler on the
connection it dialled, and either firing **closes that MQTT connection's
socket** - `c.rawConn.Close()` only, leaving the ordered teardown to `readLoop`,
exactly as the CONNECT deadline does.

The cost is that an MQTT connection does not survive a transient NATS outage.
